Title: Sell achievements, not slander: Asyraf Wajdi outlines BN's Melaka election strategy
Article:
MASJID TANAH: Barisan Nasional (BN) campaign machinery has been reminded to focus on the coalition's track record and policy offers to the people during the Melaka election campaign, rather than resorting to emotional appeals, slander or personal attacks against political opponents.
Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said campaigning should centre on explaining the agenda for the people and the state government's achievements over the past four years.
"We are accountable for our performance, not for playing on emotions. We do not need to hurl insults at others or spread slander.
"We should focus on explaining the agenda we want to implement for the people and what we have achieved over the past four years," he said at a meet-and-greet programme with the Taboh Naning state constituency community at the Cherana Puteh polling district centre here today.
Also present was incumbent Taboh Naning assemblyman Datuk Zulkiflee Mohd Zin.
On another matter, Asyraf said cooperation between BN and Perikatan Nasional (PN) in the Melaka election had shown positive progress, with both coalitions' campaign machinery working together at the grassroots level.
"This cooperation is not only at the top leadership level, but also at the division, constituency and supporters' levels. I believe this shows that the grassroots genuinely want this cooperation," he said.
He said the joint BN-PN manifesto, which was initially expected to be launched earlier, had been postponed to Tuesday to allow both coalitions to align their respective offers and agendas.
Asyraf also reminded campaign machinery not to underestimate the competition, urging them to continue engaging with all voter groups regardless of race, age or political leanings ahead of polling on Nov 14.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ab Rauf: Melaka voters, not political rivals, will judge state govt's performance
Article:
MELAKA: Melaka Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh maintains that the state government's performance should be measured and judged by the people, not its political rivals.
"I don't know where he (Melaka Pakatan Harapan (PH) chairman Adly Zahari) obtained those findings, but I don't want to comment because he was also once the Chief Minister, and I don't want to comment on what he did during his tenure either.
"So, it is better for us to reflect on ourselves and what we have done for the people. I believe the people of Melaka know what we have done. The only person who doesn't know is him," he said during a visit to the BN operations room for the Telok Mas state constituency here today.
Earlier, Adly had questioned the performance of the BN-led Melaka government despite securing a strong mandate by winning 21 of the 28 seats in the previous state election.
Adly said BN should explain its achievements during its term in office instead of merely asking voters to continue placing their trust in the administration without addressing their grievances.
He said the mandate, which gave BN nearly 75 per cent of the state seats, should have translated into solutions to the people's problems, particularly those involving housing, welfare and employment opportunities.
He also claimed that recurring floods, drainage systems, street lighting and maintenance of public facilities, particularly Melaka Sentral, remained unresolved issues affecting the people.
Ab Rauf, who is the incumbent Bukit Katil assemblyman, said Adly should reflect on his own record.
"Let others engage in (dirty politics). We will focus on talking about what we have done for the people and what they have gained from our administration of the state over the past five years.
"I noticed that the overwhelming support shown by the people yesterday during nomination day, with thousands turning up, reflected strong enthusiasm for us to return to power," he said.
Ab Rauf stressed that BN had started engaging with the people well before the election campaign and did not wait until the 14-day campaigning period to reach out to voters or make promises.

Title: Shahrizat says BN reps must serve beyond election periods
Article:
KOTA MELAKA: Veteran Umno leader Tan Sri Shahrizat Abdul Jalil has called on Barisan Nasional (BN) representatives to continue serving their constituents between elections, citing Duyong incumbent Mohd Noor Helmy as an example.
Shahrizat, an Umno Supreme Council member, said Mohd Noor Helmy remained accessible to residents and continued addressing their concerns throughout his term.
She said residents she met during a visit to Duyong had spontaneously expressed support for the incumbent, whom she described as hardworking and consistently present on the ground.
"It is not because he is an influencer. There are many influencers, but what makes him stand out is that he works hard, goes to the ground and engages with the people, not just during elections," she said.
"From what we have seen, whenever he hears about a case, he immediately goes there. He does not know the meaning of being tired," she added after visiting Duyong for the 'Ziarah HAWAcare' programme.
The visit included engagements with three residents and their families facing various difficulties, including loss of household income and serious health issues.
Also present were Wanita Umno chief Datuk Seri Dr Noraini Ahmad, Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi's wife, Datin Seri Hamidah Khamis, and BN candidate Datuk Mohd Noor Helmy Abdul Halem.
Shahrizat, who had served several terms as a member of parliament, said BN's political culture had always been to serve the people immediately after receiving their mandate.
She said this applied to both state and parliamentary elections, as public support depended on voters' views of a party's manifesto, services, policies and leadership.
"We cannot become representatives who only appear during election season. That is not our culture. You have to sacrifice your time, energy and other commitments for them," she said.
Asked whether Mohd Noor Helmy's approach could serve as an example for other BN representatives, Shahrizat said his standard of service could be emulated beyond Melaka.
"His legacy and standard of service can be an example not just for Melaka, but for the whole country," she said.
Mohd Noor Helmy said his priorities for Duyong would remain focused on residents' immediate needs, including household welfare, safety and basic infrastructure.
He said the rising cost of daily necessities, road conditions, drainage and flood prevention were more pressing concerns for residents than large-scale development projects that might not necessarily benefit the constituency.
Any development plans, he added, must take Duyong's needs into account. He would speak up against projects that were unsuitable for the area.
Of the 28 seats, 11 will see straight fights, with nine featuring contests between BN and Pakatan Harapan and the remaining two between BN and Bersatu. All 11 were won by BN in 2021.

Title: Klang's Little India bustling despite rain ahead of Deepavali
Article:
KLANG: Hindu devotees are braving the rain to finish their Deepavali shopping at Klang's Little India ahead of the celebrations on Nov 8.
A Bernama survey today found the enclave, which is home to more than 100 shops, crowded with shoppers buying clothes, jewellery, food and prayer items for the Festival of Lights.
Many visitors also spent the weekend exploring the commercial district with their families, while traders offered discounts.
Engineer S. Meiyarasan, 28, said his family had opted for last-minute shopping while keeping an eye on Klang's weather, which usually brings afternoon downpours.
"Living in Puchong, I check weather updates before travelling anywhere because of the ongoing northeast monsoon season.
"This helps ensure our shopping trip for festive essentials, especially clothes and food, goes smoothly. There is also a wide variety of items at reasonable prices here," he said.
S. Kalaiselvi, 55, described the area as a one-stop destination for Deepavali preparations, saying shopping there had been a family tradition for 20 years. She preferred shopping in person to buying online.
"I prefer shopping in person so I can check the quality and material, especially for festive attire such as sarees and dhotis for the family.
"Rain may cause some inconvenience, but completing our preparations is important for a festival celebrated only once a year," said the mother of two.
Sri Kumaran Textile owner N. Ravi Chandran, 62, said his store had extended its opening hours until midnight to cater to high customer demand, despite afternoon rain.
"Mornings are usually clear or hot, but afternoon rain means we have to keep the shop open until midnight. Nearly 2,000 customers visit, particularly at weekends.
"The festive atmosphere in the final week before Deepavali has become lively, with discounts ranging from 30 to 50 per cent. We have 35 staff members to manage the demand," he said.
Former factory worker M. Sarkunan, 66, said Klang's Little India had long been his preferred shopping destination because of its affordable prices, particularly for B40 households buying clothes and festive treats such as murukku and suji biscuits.
"Prices here are more than 10 per cent cheaper, which helps me save before I return to celebrate at my child's house in Kulim, Kedah," said the grandfather of two from Kapar.— BERNAMA

Title: BN began engaging voters long before Melaka polls, says Ab Rauf
Article:
MELAKA: The first day of campaigning for the 16th Melaka election was relatively calmer than previous elections, says Melaka Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh.
He attributed this to BN's early efforts to engage with the people, rather than limiting its outreach to the 14-day campaign period.
"We have started our work earlier so that the people are not only given attention during elections, particularly throughout the 14-day campaign period.
"Therefore, we must regard the position of an elected representative as a trust to serve the people, not for the people to serve us," he said.
He was speaking during a visit to the BN operations room for the Telok Mas state constituency here today.
Ab Rauf said the Wakil Rakyat Untuk Rakyat (WRUR) programme had resolved about 75 per cent of the 4,800 complaints received.
He said he had also stressed the importance of BN candidates understanding the people's needs before being elected as their representatives.
"Among the things I emphasised in my vision for selecting candidates to become elected representatives is that they must first be part of the people.
"They need to understand the people's problems and needs, listen to their views and convey them to me so that the government can formulate appropriate policies in the future.
"Through the WRUR programme, we successfully identified 1,001 problems and resolved about 75 per cent of the 4,800 complaints received, based on the people's needs," he said.
Commenting further, Ab Rauf said the calm campaign atmosphere should not be marred by what he described as the politics of hatred played by his opponents.
Instead, Melaka BN would continue using the campaign period to engage with voters and explain the state government's achievements.
"Let others do that. We will focus on talking about what we have implemented for the people and the benefits they have received throughout our five years administering the state," he said.

Title: Nga: Housing must put people and communities first
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Housing development must prioritise affordability, liveability and community well-being rather than treating homes as commercial commodities, Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming said.
Nga, who is also president of the United Nations Human Settlements Programme (UN-Habitat) Assembly, said urban progress should not be measured solely by the number of skyscrapers, but by improvements in community well-being.
He said this required a focus on four key pillars: affordability, liveability, connectivity and access to essential amenities.
"Housing should not merely be treated as a commodity for buying and selling but as a place where every family can build a secure and stable life. We must not only ensure that people can afford to buy a home, but also that they can live with peace of mind, comfort and dignity," he said.
He was speaking at the World Cities Day 2026 Forum on "Building High Quality Housing for the People" in Fuzhou, China.
Nga said meeting these benchmarks required coordinated action by governments, builders, developers and the wider community.
He said people-centred urban planning should combine housing with public transport, schools, medical centres and recreational spaces to build connected communities.
"Good housing must be supported by the facilities and services people need. High-rise buildings alone cannot create a community without human connection," he said.
Nga urged municipal authorities and builders to adopt artificial intelligence, green building frameworks and smart construction technologies to improve building quality, energy efficiency and resilience to climate disruptions and natural hazards.
He said urban development should be judged by improvements in people's quality of life, rather than the number of skyscrapers built.
On regional cooperation, he said the Ipoh Accord, established at the Fourth Asean-China Ministerial Roundtable on Construction and Housing in Perak on Aug 1, underpinned cross-border initiatives in low-carbon design, urban renewal and community environment upgrading.
Nga said he was confident that Malaysia-China and Asean-China partnerships would drive sustainable development for future generations.
"We do not inherit the Earth from our ancestors; we borrow it from our children. The homes and communities we build today must serve not only the present generation but also those to come," he said.

Title: Thousands protest in India's capital against voter roll revision
Article:
NEW DELHI: Thousands joined a protest led by opposition politicians in India's capital on Sunday, renewing demands for the country's election chief to resign over an overhaul of voter lists they say unfairly benefits the ruling party.
The nationwide revision of electoral rolls has sparked political disputes and street protests in the world's largest democracy over the last month.
The Election Commission says the initiative is necessary to ensure accurate voter lists, but the opposition claims it is being manipulated to favour Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).
Both the Election Commission and the BJP deny the accusations.
On Sunday, protesters led by opposition Congress party leader Rahul Gandhi chanted "vote thief, leave your seat" and beat drums while marching from central parts of New Delhi to Ramlila Maidan, a large outdoor venue.
"I have been a voter since I was 18 and now I find myself struck off the list," protester Nandita, 46, told AFP, giving only one name.
"It's important to be here because of the way things are going. The cost of living is going up... The only option is to take to the streets peacefully."
The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), an online youth-led protest movement, has also thrown its weight behind the campaign against the voter-roll revision.
The overhaul of India's voter rolls has resulted in more than 133 million names being removed from electoral lists, according to figures reported by Indian media and cited by opposition parties in court filings.
Critics say the removals have disproportionately affected minorities, particularly Muslims.
[[nid:1568447]]
Members of Hindu-nationalist BJP have long alleged that large numbers of undocumented Muslim migrants from neighbouring Bangladesh have fraudulently entered India's electoral rolls.
Election authorities say the revision was intended to eliminate duplicate, deceased and fraudulent entries, and that eligible voters remain entitled to apply for inclusion on the roll.
Human Rights Watch has said the removal of voters was "arbitrary and deeply flawed."
"The authorities should immediately scrap the voter roll revision process that has denied India's most marginalised people their right to vote and other government services," it said in a statement this week.
The Cockroach movement has been heavily involved in the pushback to the voter-roll revision and several of its leaders were temporarily detained by police during protests last month.
The CJP has gained millions of followers on social media since it was launched in May.
Earlier protests organised by the CJP in July over exam irregularities forced the resignation of the education minister, marking a rare climbdown by Modi's administration.

Title: With no majority, what options remain for Israel's Netanyahu, Eisenkot?
Article:
FOLLOWING elections in which Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his main rival Gadi Eisenkot both fell short of a majority, each is claiming a mandate to govern – though neither has explained how.
Given the indecisive result, the two leaders would need to find a way to broaden their blocs if they hope to secure a governing coalition, but so far very little information has leaked about potential behind-the-scenes negotiations.
If neither succeeds in securing a coalition, the country will have to head back to the polls.
AFP looks at the most plausible scenarios for each side forming a government.
A Netanyahu-led government
The prime minister and his far-right and ultra-Orthodox allies came out ahead in the final vote count, with 53 seats in parliament, including 27 for the premier's party, Likud.
But that is still short of the 61 needed for a majority.
If he hopes to stay in power, Netanyahu will have to reach out to opposition parties with a pitch to join his government – a major about-face after a campaign run on vows to unseat him.
Israeli President Isaac Herzog, who is tasked with tapping the candidate best positioned to form a coalition, has said a new vote must be avoided at all costs.
Of the four parties in Eisenkot's camp, the least receptive to an overture from Netanyahu would be the left-wing Democrats, led by Yair Golan, which won eight seats.
Netanyahu's former ally turned fierce critic Avigdor Lieberman, whose right-wing Yisrael Beiteinu party won seven seats, would also likely dismiss the prospect out of hand.
Lieberman said on Thursday that "the only conceivable coalition" was one without Netanyahu, though he suggested the rest of the premier's party would be tolerated.
The stance of Naftali Bennett's centre-right Together party, which won 12 seats, is less clear.
Bennett had initially suggested he would not oppose an alliance with Netanyahu's camp under certain conditions, notably the immediate creation of a commission of inquiry into the Oct 7, 2023 attacks.
But he later backtracked and insisted his remarks had been misconstrued.
Finally, the possibility of an alliance with Eisenkot's Yashar party, which nabbed 21 seats, seems remote given the ex-general built his campaign around promises to remove Netanyahu, who he said was unfit to lead.
There is a recent precedent for unlikely power-sharing scenarios. In 2020, Netanyahu and centrist Benny Gantz overcame their deep antipathy to strike a deal to rotate the prime ministership, but the partnership collapsed after a year.
Eisenkot has repeatedly ruled out such an arrangement, saying before the vote: "There will be no form of rotation in the post of prime minister. There will be only one prime minister, and it will be me."
[[nid:1568434]]
Outside the opposition camp, there remains the highly improbable option of Netanyahu turning to Arab-majority lists, with their 19 seats.
The prime minister spent the campaign casting them as bogeymen, and in the days since the vote has accused them of electoral fraud.
But nothing is out of the question when it comes to Netanyahu, a canny political operator who reached out to Arab parties in 2015 and 2021.
An Eisenkot-led government
By refusing to deliver a majority to Netanyahu's camp, the Israeli people "have chosen change", Eisenkot proclaimed on election night.
With his camp holding 48 seats, and having ruled out a power-sharing deal with Netanyahu, Eisenkot has two options going forward: establishing a minority government supported from the outside by other parties, or attempting to broaden his coalition by bringing in Arab lawmakers or defectors from the other camp.
The two Arab-majority groupings, Raam and the Joint List, emerged with eight and 11 seats, respectively.
Raam leader Mansour Abbas joined a short-lived coalition once before, and has voiced willingness to do so again, but that option is opposed by some parties in the opposition bloc.
The Joint List's Yousef Jabareen, meanwhile, has said he is willing to support Eisenkot in parliament but without joining his government, expressing discomfort with, among other things, the war in Gaza.
Taken together, the Arab lists would give Eisenkot the seats he needs to move forward, but relying on them would mean going back on a campaign promise and gambling on a fragile minority government that observers say would be unlikely to last long.
A former army chief, Eisenkot is not a pacifist, and the possibility of future military operations – including in Gaza, where he has pledged to end Hamas rule in 18 months – could prompt his new allies to pull their support.
Eisenkot could also try to woo away defectors from Netanyahu's camp.
Defections from the Likud are improbable given how firmly the party is aligned behind the premier, and its far-right allies are considered politically unpalatable to the change bloc.
But the remaining ultra-Orthodox parties currently aligned with Netanyahu, who hold 13 seats, could prove more amenable.
Eisenkot – who lost a son in the Gaza war – has argued forcefully for ending military service exemptions for the ultra-Orthodox community, which those parties oppose, though they could be willing to jump ship in the event of concessions from one side or the other.
* The article is from AFP

Title: Zahid: BN ready to invite PN to join state gov't if it wins Melaka polls
Article:
BAGAN DATUK: Barisan Nasional is prepared to invite Perikatan Nasional to join the state administration if the coalition succeeds in forming the government following the 16th Melaka election on Nov 14.
BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the approach was taken to respect the people's mandate and the political understanding reached between the two coalitions, similar to what had previously been implemented in Negeri Sembilan.
"As happened in Negri Sembilan, when the government was formed, we honoured the appointments to ensure that they (PN) were part of the government.
"The same happened in Melaka when the previous Unity Government was formed, with our partners in PH (Pakatan Harapan) also appointed as state executive councillors and deputy exco members, but they subsequently decided to leave.
"So we will do the same for PN assemblymen who win their respective seats and, God willing, if we form the government, we will also invite them to be part of the state government," he told reporters after attending the 2026 Deepavali Santunan Kasih event at Dewan Umno Bagan Datuk here.
In this election, BN is contesting 23 of the 28 seats up for grabs, while PN is contesting five seats.
The Election Commission has set Nov 14 as polling day for the Melaka state election, while early voting will take place on Nov 10. - BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar joins MotoGP fans as Marc Marquez claims Malaysian GP victory
Article:
SEPANG: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim spent time watching the 2026 Malaysian Motorcycle Grand Prix (MotoGP) at the Sepang International Circuit (SIC) here today.
Youth and Sports Minister Dr Mohammed Taufiq Johari and SIC chief executive officer Azhan Shafriman Hanif welcomed Anwar upon his arrival.
He was then taken on a tour of the K2 Hillstand spectator seating area before heading to the starting grid to mingle with spectators ahead of the MotoGP race, which began at 3pm.
The atmosphere at the circuit was further enlivened by a rendition of the national anthem, Negaraku, by national songstress Datuk Seri Siti Nurhaliza Tarudin.
Ducati Lenovo Team rider Marc Marquez emerged victorious in today's race, followed by Pedro Acosta of Red Bull KTM Factory Racing in second place and Alex Marquez of BK8 Gresini Racing MotoGP in third.
The victory saw Marc Marquez strengthen his position at the top of the 2026 MotoGP world championship standings with 399 points, extending his lead over closest challenger Jorge Martin of Aprilia Racing to 44 points. Martin has 355 points.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 9-year-old wins NSTP colouring contest at Jom Heboh
Article:
JOHOR BARU: A chance stop at the New Straits Times Press (NSTP) booth at Karnival Jom Heboh turned into a winning moment for a 9-year-old boy who took first prize in a colouring contest.
Tunku Mohamad Aisy Sufi Tunku Muhamad Naufal, from Larkin, had only intended to take a short break with his family when he spotted the contest at the NSTP booth at Padang B, Angsana Johor Baru Mall, here today.
His mother, Rohana Ahmad, 39, said her son, who enjoyed colouring and frequently took part in similar competitions, decided to join on the spur of the moment.
"He had been looking forward to KJH for some time, but we did not know there was a colouring contest at the NSTP booth.
"We happened to walk past and wanted to stop for shelter. When he found out about the contest, he was excited and immediately signed up. We never expected him to win first place," she said after the prize presentation at the booth today.
Rohana said future contests should be publicised earlier to allow children to prepare and bring their own colouring materials.
Tunku Mohamad Aisy Sufi won prizes worth RM250, presented by NSTP Senior Executive Officer of the Branding and Intellectual Property Department Wan Fazly Hizam Wan Kadir.
Adwa Zakwan, 7, from Taman Perling, took second place with prizes worth RM200, while Muhammad Yusuf Iskandar Mohd Zulfazli, 6, from Skudai, inished third, taking home prizes worth RM150.
NSTP Branding and Intellectual Property Department head Tengku Kaifimirza Tuan Cherit @ Tengku Hamzah said the booth had received an encouraging response from visitors since the event began on Friday.
He said the initiative aimed to entertain children while building familiarity with the NSTP brand among younger generations.
"Our main aim is to make parents happy by giving their children an enjoyable experience, while bringing the NSTP brand closer to families, especially the younger generation," he said.
He thanked Econsave for sponsoring the competition prizes.
Participants also received complimentary goodie bags containing products sponsored by Julie's, Nestle, Yakult and Nibou, as well as colouring pencils and storybooks from the Penang Public Library.

Title: "Sometimes, I feel like giving up": Traders struggle with rising costs
Article:
KAJANG: Small-scale traders are hoping the government will address rising costs, modest earnings and weak consumer spending following its call to assess their incomes.
Traditional kuih seller Aina Nabilah Abdul Malek, 32, said she had turned to providing e-hailing services for women to supplement her earnings from the business she started in 2022.
Based in Bandar Sri Permaisuri, Cheras, she said her monthly earnings fluctuated, sometimes exceeding RM1,000 and sometimes falling below that amount.
"Sometimes, I feel like giving up because the income is low, but I am passionate about making kuih and still have the drive to keep going," she said when met at the market held in conjunction with the 2026 National Hawkers and Small Traders Day.
Aina said rising ingredient costs and limited room to raise prices had squeezed her earnings, while difficulties with social media marketing meant she relied on face-to-face sales.
"I can't charge too much for my kuih or people won't buy them. I also have to make, market and sell them myself, so any help with marketing would make a big difference," she said.
For crochet trader Asfaniza Mohd Jaffar, 49, attracting customers willing to pay for handmade products remained a challenge.
[[nid:1568409]]
She said some visitors browsed without buying, as tight household budgets meant non-essential purchases such as handicrafts had to wait.
"My earnings are very modest, although sales tend to improve around payday or festive periods," she said, adding that cheaper imported products also posed stiff competition.
Asfaniza urged Kuskop to provide marketing support and help traders participate in larger events to reach more customers.
Federation of Malay Hawkers and Petty Traders Associations Malaysia president Datuk Zainal Abidin Abd Majid welcomed Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's emphasis on improving traders' incomes.
He said the federation was working with the Implementation Coordination Unit of the Prime Minister's Department to provide traders nationwide with tools to boost productivity and income.
Zainal also welcomed the RM1 million allocation announced by Anwar to the Entrepreneur Development and Cooperatives Ministry (Kuskop) to coordinate assistance for hawker and petty trader associations.
"I believe this contribution will enable us to continue our efforts to help B40 hawkers progress," he said, adding that the federation hoped to help them move out of the income group and strengthen their families' finances.
Earlier, Anwar called on Kuskop Minister Steven Sim to work with trader associations to compare their average incomes with levels three years ago and identify shortcomings in existing support.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Hadi visits Tun M, offers condolences over Siti Hasmah's passing
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Pas president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang visited Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad at the former prime minister's residence in Seri Kembangan this morning.
In a Facebook post today, Abdul Hadi said he prayed for Dr Mahathir to remain patient following the death of his wife, Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohamad Ali, on Sept 28.
He also prayed for the late Dr Siti Hasmah to continue receiving Allah's blessings.
"I conveyed to Tun Dr Mahathir a hadith of Prophet Muhammad SAW.
"Indeed, to Allah belongs what He takes and to Him belongs what He gives. Everything has an appointed time. So be patient and hope for Allah's reward," he said.
Dr Siti Hasmah died at the National Heart Institute (IJN) on Sept 28 at the age of 100.
She was laid to rest with a state dignitary's funeral ceremony at Makam Pusara Negara in Precinct 20, Putrajaya.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Husband, wife killed after tar-laden lorry crushes MPV in Batu Pahat
Article:
BATU PAHAT: A husband and wife were killed while their two children survived after a lorry carrying tar overturned and crushed their multi-purpose vehicle (MPV) along Jalan Yong Peng-Muar near Kampung Sri Wangi, Parit Yaani, at noon today.
The crash is believed to have occurred around 12.15pm, killing Mohd Hardi Mohd Husin, 46, and his wife, Tengku Syafirana Tengku Abdullah, 44, at the scene.
Their two children, an 8-year-old boy and an 11-year-old girl, were injured and are receiving treatment at the Sultanah Nora Ismail Hospital here.
Yong Peng Fire and Rescue Station operations commander Mohamad Alif Halim said the department received an emergency call at 12.24pm and dispatched six firefighters to the scene.
He said the team found a 10-tonne Hino lorry and a Perodua Alza involved in the crash.
"The Alza was carrying four people, comprising a 46-year-old male driver and a 44-year-old female passenger, both of whom were trapped, while the two children sustained minor injuries.
"The 30-year-old lorry driver was also injured. Firefighters carried out a rescue operation to extricate the trapped victims using specialised equipment.
"Those who sustained minor injuries were given initial treatment before being handed over to medical personnel, while the deceased were handed over to the police for further action," he said.
Batu Pahat police chief Assistant Commissioner Shahrulanuar Mushaddat Abdullah Sani confirmed the incident when contacted.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Indonesia's forest fire hotspots fall to 96, peat fire risks persist
Article:
JAKARTA: Indonesia's forest and land fire hotspots have declined to 96 from 160 a day earlier, but rising detections in Central Kalimantan and persistent underground peat fires continue to pose challenges to firefighting efforts.
The Forestry Ministry said high-confidence hotspots declined by 64 nationwide as of 9pm on Saturday, although Central Kalimantan recorded an increase from 12 to 15 hotspots.
Of the 96 hotspots detected nationwide, 19 were recorded across six priority provinces, comprising 15 in Central Kalimantan, three in South Sumatra and one in South Kalimantan.
"Central Kalimantan remains one of the main priorities in forest and land fire control efforts.
"The nature of peatlands means firefighting operations take longer, as fires can continue burning and spreading underground even after surface flames have been extinguished or rainfall has occurred," it said in its latest update posted on Instagram on Sunday.
The ministry said Forestry Minister Raja Juli Antoni had inspected previously affected areas in Central Kalimantan to assess conditions and ensure continued monitoring and enforcement.
A total of 61 aircraft remained deployed for firefighting operations, including 24 for aerial patrols and weather modification, and 37 helicopters for water bombing.
The ministry urged communities and businesses to avoid using fire to clear land and to report any signs of smoke or burning.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Yayasan JCorp, UTHM join hands to preserve Johor's traditional music
Article:
BATU PAHAT: Yayasan Johor Corporation (Yayasan JCorp) and Universiti Tun Hussein Onn Malaysia (UTHM) have forged a strategic partnership to preserve Johor's traditional musical heritage, particularly Ghazal and Gambus, and ensure its continuity among future generations.
Yayasan JCorp chief executive officer Datuk Mizan Yahya said the collaboration, formalised through a letter of intent (LOI), would cover training, workshops, historical documentation and the sharing of stage performance techniques.
He said the partnership would link live performances with long-term efforts to nurture talent, document artistic knowledge and ensure the traditions continued to be practised and passed down.
"We do not want the public's connection with Ghazal and Gambus to end the moment the stage lights go out. Our aspiration is for more young people to take an interest in learning these traditions, for more practitioners to share their knowledge, and for a greater wealth of artistic heritage to be documented and passed down to future generations.
"Festivals will continue to be organised to spark interest, and such collaborations help translate that interest into sustained community engagement," he told Bernama after the LOI exchange in conjunction with the Jelajah Pentas Seni Johor 2026 (PSJ26) tour at Dataran Astaka Shahbandar.
The LOI exchange between Mizan, representing Yayasan JCorp, and UTHM Centre for General Studies and Co-curriculum (PPUK) Dean Dr Zahrul Akmal Damin was witnessed by Batu Pahat Municipal Council (MPBP) president Mohd Nazid Jasiman.
Mizan said the Batu Pahat leg was the third stop of the PSJ26 tour, following earlier events in Pontian and Segamat, and aimed to bring arts and heritage closer to the community.
"In Pontian, we held the Festival Rumpun Bugis Johor, while in Segamat, the programme featured the Festival Kota Selatan.
"Here in Batu Pahat, we are highlighting local community culture, blending the melodic rhythms of Ghazal and Gambus with the culinary delights of Nasi Ambeng and Sambal Goreng Jawa.
"The festivities here are enlivened by performances such as Zapin Koris, Zapin Tanjung Laboh, Zapin Duo Batu Pahat, acrobatic dragon dances, Gambus music and a Shariah-compliant version of the Kuda Kepang dance," he said.
The PSJ26 tour will continue in Kota Tinggi on Nov 28 and 29 before concluding in Johor Baru in December.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Immigration: Report alleged Special Pass irregularities directly to authorities
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Immigration Department has urged the public to report alleged irregularities in the issuance of Special Passes involving its officers in Kuala Lumpur directly to the authorities.
Immigration director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said information or evidence could be submitted to Immigration or the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) to facilitate a comprehensive investigation.
"Providing information directly to the authorities is crucial to protecting the confidentiality of information and preserving the integrity of evidence.
"Publicly disclosing information about suspected unlawful activities before reporting it to the authorities could prompt those involved to halt their activities, change their modus operandi or destroy evidence, thereby hindering investigations and enforcement action," he said in a statement today.
Zakaria said the department viewed the allegations seriously and would not tolerate misconduct, abuse of power or breaches of integrity by its officers, regardless of rank or position.
As part of efforts to strengthen integrity and accountability, Zakaria said a total of 849 immigration officers had faced disciplinary action from 2023 to October this year, including 73 who were dismissed.
From January to October this year alone, 96 officers faced disciplinary action, including 18 who were dismissed.
He said the figures reflected the department's firm stance on taking action against officers found to have committed disciplinary offences.
Immigration would continue to strengthen integrity, procedural compliance and internal controls to ensure that all services were delivered transparently and in accordance with the law, he added. —  BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Over 800 teachers martyred in Gaza, Palestinian official says
Article:
TEHERAN: More than 800 teachers have been martyred in the Gaza Strip since October 2023, said a Palestinian education official.
He described the targeting of teachers as an attack on the future of Palestinian generations and their right to education and life, Islamic Republic News Agency (IRNA) reported.
The head of public relations at the Palestinian Ministry of Education in Gaza, Ahmad al-Najjar said on Sunday that Israeli occupying forces continue to target educational staff in the Gaza Strip.
The official cited the martyrdom of several teachers in recent days as part of ongoing crimes against education personnel.
According to the latest figures released by the ministry, more than 800 teachers, both men and women, have been martyred and over 3,300 others injured since the onset of the devastating war in October 2023.
The ministry called on the international community, United Nations agencies and human rights organisations to take immediate action to stop these crimes, hold those responsible accountable, and ensure the safety of civilians and education personnel.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Mata Ayer assemblyman Wan Badariah laid to rest
Article:
ARAU: Mata Ayer assemblyman Wan Badariah Wan Saad,  who died at Tuanku Fauziah Hospital (HTF) in Kangar yesterday afternoon, was laid to rest today. She was 50.
Wan Badariah was buried at the Kampung Rambai Muslim Cemetery at 11.50am.
Earlier, funeral prayers for the assemblyman were performed at Masjid Nur Al-Saadah in Kampung Banggol Sena here about 11am, led by the mosque's Imam I, Amirul Hadafi Raseli, and attended by approximately 500 people, including family members, residents; and Pas and Bersatu elected representatives.
Among the Pas representatives who attended the funeral prayers were former Perlis Menteri Besar and Sanglang assemblyman Mohd Shukri Ramli, Santan assemblyman Muhammad Azmir Azizan and Kayang assemblyman Asrul Aimran Abd Jalil.
Bersatu was represented by its Perlis leadership body chairman Izizam Ibrahim, who is also the Titi Tinggi assemblyman.
Wan Badariah died at HTF at 4.26pm.
In the 15th general election (GE15), Wan Badariah, who contested under the Perikatan Nasional (PN) ticket, secured 4,419 votes, defeating Barisan Nasional (BN) candidate Siti Berenee Yahaya, who obtained 2,398 votes, and Amran Kamarudin of Pakatan Harapan (PH), who received 794 votes, with a majority of 2,021 votes.
She previously served as Perlis Tourism, Culture, Arts and Heritage Committee chairman under the administration of menteri besar Shukri. — BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Halloween party at unlicensed entertainment outlet ends with eight arrests
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Eight men, including six foreigners, were arrested when police raided an unlicensed entertainment outlet hosting a Halloween party along Jalan Tun Razak early today.
The raid, conducted under Op Noda between 2am and 5am, involved officers from the Wangsa Maju police headquarters' Anti-Vice, Gambling and Secret Societies Division (D7) and Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department.
Wangsa Maju police chief Assistant Commissioner Annas Sulaiman said preliminary investigations found that the premises had been operating without a valid entertainment licence.
He said the outlet was decorated with Halloween-themed props, while patrons were enjoying loud music and alcoholic drinks when police arrived.
Eight men aged between 21 and 40 were detained, including a 22-year-old local man working as the outlet's cashier and another local customer.
The other six foreigners comprised two Bangladeshis, two Myanmar citizens who did not possess valid travel documents, and two Chinese citizens.
Annas said questioning revealed that the cashier had been working at the premises for six months but claimed he was unaware of its licensing status.
"Police also seized various audio equipment, including two Pioneer multi-player DJ units, microphones, speakers and amplifiers, as well as four bottles of liquor of various brands and business sales receipts.
"The total value of the seized items is estimated at more than RM2,100," he said.
He added that an incident occurred during the raid in which a suspect allegedly attempted to obstruct civil servants from carrying out their duties.
All suspects and seized items were taken to the Wangsa Maju police headquarters and handed over to investigating officer Inspector Aliff Sazrie Azmi for further action.
The case is being investigated under Section 4(1) of the Federal Territory Entertainment Act, Sections 6(1)(c) and 39(b) of the Immigration Act 1959/63, Regulation 25 of the National Registration Regulations 1990, and Section 186 of the Penal Code for obstructing a public servant.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: PDAM calls for probe into entire fuel supply chain over possible RON95 contamination
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Petrol Dealers Association of Malaysia (PDAM) has urged the Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry to investigate the entire fuel supply chain to determine the cause of recent RON95 petrol contamination reports and vehicle damage.
Its president, Datuk Khairul Annuar Abdul Aziz, said the investigation should cover storage depots and the delivery process, rather than being limited to inspections at petrol stations.
"PDAM notes that the ministry's preliminary inspections in early October at 11 petrol stations in Kedah and six in Perak found no indication of water in their underground storage tanks.
"However, these findings are preliminary and limited to the stations inspected. They cannot be considered conclusive pending further laboratory analysis," he said in a statement today.
Khairul Annuar said PDAM welcomed a wider investigation covering the entire fuel supply chain, including storage depots and delivery processes, to identify the actual source of any contamination.
He stressed that petrol station operators did not produce or mix the fuel, but relied entirely on their respective oil companies to supply petrol that met the required specifications.
He also strongly rejected claims that petrol station operators deliberately mixed water into petrol to make extra profits.
"Such actions offer no economic benefit to operators. Instead, they could damage vehicles, undermine customer confidence and hurt their businesses.
"Any fuel quality issue must be determined through an independent investigation into the relevant supply chain, rather than immediately placing the blame on petrol station operators," he said.
PDAM also urged affected consumers to lodge official complaints directly with the ministry and the relevant oil companies, instead of circulating unverified claims on social media.
Khairul Annuar said social media accusations identifying specific petrol stations could cause public concern and damage the reputation of operators who were not at fault.
He advised operators who had been targeted by defamatory or false accusations to keep evidence and lodge police reports for further action, including referring cases to the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC).
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Azalina backs wider CSA to push institutional reforms through Parliament
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Broader cooperation between government and opposition lawmakers under the Confidence and Supply Agreement (CSA) could help secure parliamentary support for key institutional reforms, including a proposed 10-year limit on the prime minister's tenure.
Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said cross-party cooperation was crucial to building parliamentary consensus on reforms, particularly the separation of the roles of attorney-general and public prosecutor.
She said political differences should not prevent lawmakers from working together to ensure national stability and safeguard the people's interests.
Azalina said expanding the agreement would allow more MPs to participate in cross-party cooperation and demonstrate maturity in parliamentary democracy.
"Political differences should not be an obstacle to cooperation for the sake of national stability and the interests of the people.
"In fact, a similar approach was implemented when Umno was part of the federal government during the previous parliamentary term," she said in a statement.
She also welcomed Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi's support for the CSA and his proposal to extend the arrangement to opposition parties.
Azalina said broader cooperation was particularly important in advancing institutional reforms that required support across party lines.
She identified the proposed separation of the roles of attorney-general and public prosecutor, as well as the plan to limit the Prime Minister's tenure to 10 years, as two major reforms that could benefit from such cooperation.
"More comprehensive cross-party cooperation is essential in building parliamentary consensus to implement institutional reforms, particularly the separation of the roles of attorney-general and public prosecutor and the proposal to limit the prime minister's tenure to 10 years," she said.
Azalina stressed that reforms involving national interests and amendments to the Federal Constitution should be thoroughly examined and supported by lawmakers from both sides of the political divide.
She said this would ensure that voters, through their elected representatives, had a say in determining the future of the country's institutions.
"Reforms involving national interests and amendments to the Federal Constitution should receive scrutiny and support across party lines.
"This is to ensure that the voices of the people, represented by their respective MPs, are involved in determining the direction and future of national institutions through debates and voting in Parliament," she said.
Azalina also reaffirmed Barisan Nasional's commitment to maintaining political stability and strengthening democratic institutions as part of the unity government.
"As part of the unity government, Barisan Nasional will continue to play a constructive role in preserving political stability, strengthening democratic institutions and ensuring the country is governed effectively for the benefit of the people," she said.
The CSA was signed on Oct 29 by 13 lawmakers, comprising six Bersatu members of parliament, Muar MP Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman and six independent MPs.
Under the agreement, the lawmakers committed to supporting the 2027 Budget and key institutional reforms, including limiting the prime minister's tenure and separating the roles of attorney-general and public prosecutor.
The arrangement also provides for constituency development allocations comparable to those received by government backbenchers.
Earlier today, DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke said his party supported the CSA, which had been agreed upon by the Pakatan Harapan (PH) presidential council.
Loke said the agreement was intended to ensure political stability and prevent attempts to bring down the government.
The proposed constitutional amendment to limit the prime minister's tenure to 10 years previously failed to secure the required two-thirds majority in the Dewan Rakyat on March 2.
The bill received 146 votes in favour, two short of the 148 required for passage, while 44 MPs abstained and 32 were absent.
The proposed separation of the attorney-general's and public prosecutor's roles has also undergone scrutiny as part of the government's institutional reform agenda.
Both reforms were among the constitutional amendment bills tabled in the Dewan Rakyat in February.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Kelantan govt allocates RM11mil to upgrade Merbau Chondong water treatment plant  - Izani
Article:
KOTA BARU: The Kelantan government has allocated RM11 million to upgrade the Merbau Chondong Water Treatment Plant (LRA) to increase its production capacity from 45 million litres to 70 million litres a day, with the project expected to be completed by January next year.
State Public Works, Infrastructure, Water and Rural Development Committee chairman Datuk Dr Izani Husin said the capacity expansion is necessary to meet the increasing demand for water, particularly in Pasir Puteh.
He said, however, that previous increases in water output from the plant had led to turbidity issues due to high levels of iron and magnesium in the raw water source.
"Through an RM11 million budget allocation, the state government has carried out improvement works on the treatment process at the Merbau Chondong LRA, and we expect water quality to improve once the project is completed," he said.
Izani was replying to a question from Nor Asilah Mohamed Zin (Pas-Limbongan) regarding the state government's efforts to address water supply and quality issues in Pasir Puteh during the Kelantan state legislative assembly sitting at the Kota Darulnaim Complex today.
In a related development, Izani said the state government is also constructing the Tok Bali LRA with a capacity of 50 million litres per day to increase the supply of treated water in Pasir Puteh.
He said physical progress on the project currently stands at 30 per cent, which is one per cent behind schedule, with completion expected by late 2028.
"Once the Tok Bali LRA is completed, 50 million litres of treated water daily will be channelled to Pasir Puteh residents, while supply from Merbau Chondong can be redistributed to meet the needs of other areas," he said.
Replying to a supplementary question from Datuk Abd Rahman Yunus (Pas-Pasir Tumboh) on the state government's achievements in improving water supply and quality, Izani said upgrading and repair works on 11 LRAs across Kelantan are also underway.
"Among the plants involved are Kuala Balah, Chicha, Pahi, and Manik Urai, at a total cost of RM3.43 million, funded through Pengurusan Aset Air Bhd (PAAB).
"The state government is also implementing rural water supply projects, including building a hill reservoir in Merbau and upgrading the pumping system at the Merbau Chondong LRA, with an allocation of RM30 million from the Rural and Regional Development Ministry," he said. — BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: RMAF's two new FA-50M jets arrive in Kuantan
Article:
KUANTAN: Two newly acquired FA-50M light combat aircraft arrived at the Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) Kuantan Air Base today.
The aircraft, developed by Korea Aerospace Industries (KAI), arrived at RMAF Labuan Air Base from South Korea on Oct 30 before flying to Kuantan about 3.40pm today.
[[nid:1568348]]
The RMAF Facebook page shared images of the aircraft on the tarmac, with a caption stating that the FA-50M aircraft, 'M58-01' and 'M58-02', had landed safely at Kuantan Air Base from Labuan.
An official handover ceremony is scheduled to take place at Kuantan Air Base in the middle of this month.
[[nid:1568347]]
They are part of an 18-unit order under Malaysia's Fighter Lead-In Training and Light Combat Aircraft programme. Deliveries of the remaining aircraft will be made in stages until early 2028.
The FA-50M fleet is expected to replace the RMAF's Hawk aircraft when they are decommissioned in 2028.
Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin, who witnessed the aircraft's arrival in Labuan, said the FA-50M would serve as both a lead-in fighter trainer and a light combat aircraft.
[[nid:1568346]]
In 2023, the Defence Ministry signed a contract worth nearly RM4 billion with KAI for the procurement of 18 FA-50 Block 20 aircraft, designated as the FA-50M.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysians face pricey Indian onions as fresh supply delays cloud Deepavali festival
Article:
PHNOM PENH: Malaysian consumers could pay more for Indian onions ahead of the Deepavali festival as production in Maharashtra, India's biggest producing state, falls nearly 40 per cent due to weak rainfall.
Irregular rainfall and prolonged dry spells this monsoon have delayed the arrival of fresh kharif onions, the monsoon-season crop, adding price pressure to local Indian markets.
"There could be about a 30 to 40 per cent production drop in Maharashtra because of drought. Farmers across India are facing a shortage of rain due to El Nino and this is impacting onion production because of poor moisture. Prices could gradually increase," Lasalgaon Agricultural Produce Market Committee Chairman Dnyaneshwar Kisan Jagtap told Bernama on Saturday.
Lasalgaon, a town in the western Indian state of Maharashtra, is home to Asia's largest onion market and serves as a key centre for setting onion prices in India.
Millions of Hindus around the world will celebrate Deepavali, the annual festival of lights on Nov 8.
Demand is likely to soar for the reddish bulb, famous for its pungency, colour and long-shelf life. It is an important ingredient in every Indian cuisine.
India is one of the largest onion-growing countries in the world after China, with annual production of about 30 million tonnes. Last year, it exported about 1.5 million metric tonnes of fresh onions, according to India's Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority.
Malaysia imports more than 50 per cent of its onion supply from India, with Maharashtra accounting for a large share of the shipments.
The state produces more than 50 per cent of India's onion exports.
Indian consumers are currently paying about 60 Indian rupees (0.63 cents/RM2.56) per kg.
Export prices range from US$500 to US$700 per metric tonne (RM2,029 to RM2,841) for standard red onions, depending on the destination, say industry players.
"We are hoping to see crop growth post-Diwali (northern Indian pronunciation of Deepavali) as there has been some rainfall in recent days.
"We can only see better improvements in the next monsoon season, in July or August," said Jagtap.
Production remains tight, and prices are volatile, while farmers are likely to face a financial crunch during the festival season.
"Around Diwali, the market is expected to remain sensitive to supply conditions. As fresh kharif arrivals increase, price pressures may ease. However, the extent of any price correction will depend on actual production, market arrivals and demand.
"Countries such as Malaysia that import Indian onions may face higher procurement costs if Indian wholesale and export prices remain elevated," Sanjay Holkar, a leading exporter based in Nashik City in Maharashtra, told Bernama.
Indian Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution Ministry, in a statement dated Oct 9, said fresh kharif onions are beginning to arrive from major producing states — including Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Rajasthan, while availability from stored stocks continues to meet market demands.
"Arrivals from these producing regions are expected to increase further in the coming weeks, improving overall availability in the consuming markets during the upcoming festive season," said the ministry.
In Kuala Lumpur, ahead of Deepavali, the Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry capped the prices of essential items including Australian dhal, grated coconut, large red onions and Indian shallots, from Nov 4 to 10.
Onion prices are currently costing about RM4 per kg in local markets.
According to the Federal Agricultural Marketing Authority, Malaysians consume nearly 750,000 metric tonnes of onions annually.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Zahid: Flood hotspots identified ahead of Northeast Monsoon
Article:
BAGAN DATUK: The government and all relevant agencies are fully prepared to face the Northeast Monsoon, which is expected to have a more severe impact than in previous years.
Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the state of preparedness involved comprehensive coordination between the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma) and disaster management committees at state and district levels, following the launch of National Preparedness Month 2026 in Ipoh last month.
"This year's Northeast Monsoon is expected to have a more severe impact than in previous years, following an El Nino episode that affected many countries, particularly in Asean.
"Nadma, in collaboration with all enforcement agencies, has identified hotspots where unusually heavy rainfall is expected," he told a press conference after attending the '2026 Deepavali Santunan Kasih' event at the Bagan Datuk Umno Hall today.
Asked whether certain states would be the main focus during the monsoon season, Zahid said Kelantan, Terengganu, the northern states, particularly Kedah, as well as southern states comprising Johor, Melaka and Negri Sembilan were frequently affected by the Northeast Monsoon.
Zahid, who is also National Disaster Management Committee chairman, said responsibilities had been assigned to rescue agencies, while the Welfare Department was prepared with stockpiles of food aid and fully equipped evacuation tents, with additional support from non-governmental organisations (NGOs).
On Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) candidates who would be sitting for their examinations during the monsoon season, he assured that the welfare of the students and the smooth conduct of their examinations remained a priority for the government.
[[nid:1568418]]
He said he had discussed the matter with Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek at a recent cabinet meeting, with contingency plans being drawn up to accommodate affected students at school hostels.
"She (Fadhlina) informed me that students in areas expected to experience severe flooding had been identified and would be relocated to schools with hostels, where they would sit for their examinations. The Examinations Board is also fully prepared for this," he said.
Meanwhile, Zahid said improvements to the Bantuan Wang Ihsan (BWI) compassionate aid scheme, introduced last year, would continue, with RM1,000 in aid channelled directly to each family while they were at temporary relief centres.
He said the measure would enable flood victims to use the assistance immediately upon returning home to clean their houses and replace damaged household items, provided they had officially relocated to a relief centre, to prevent leakages.
He said flood victims previously had to wait two weeks and visit a bank to collect the assistance, but under the new arrangement, the RM1,000 would be handed to them directly once they were at the relief centres.
"However, those who do not relocate, even if their names are on the list, will not receive the assistance.
"They must move to a relief centre to ensure the funds are not misappropriated or channelled to other parties," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Indonesians make up 79pct of Johor's foreign patients
Article:
ISKANDAR PUTERI: Johor is looking to attract more Indonesian visitors, particularly medical tourists, with a new ferry link to Batam expected to improve cross-border connectivity and create fresh tourism opportunities.
Indonesians accounted for 79 per cent of the 127,000 international patients treated in Johor in 2025, while about 1.5 million Indonesians visited the state that year.
Indonesian Consul-General in Johor Baru Sigit Suryantoro Widiyanto said the new service linking Puteri Harbour International Ferry Terminal with Gold Coast Ferry Terminal in Bengkong, Batam, would make travel more convenient for visitors from both sides.
He said the route would particularly benefit those travelling to western Batam, an area experiencing growing tourism development.
"For Johoreans travelling to Batam, this provides another option. Likewise, visitors from Batam coming to Johor will find it more convenient to reach attractions such as Johor Premium Outlets and Legoland.
"This will certainly open up new opportunities," he said after attending the launch of the ferry service today.
The route, introduced by B Ferry, is expected to strengthen tourism ties while creating opportunities in trade, services and local businesses.
Sigit said ferry connectivity remained a major driver of travel between the two countries, particularly between Johor and Indonesia's Riau Islands.
Of the 11 passenger ferry connections between Indonesia and Malaysia, eight operated through Johor, while the remaining services served destinations in Kalimantan, Port Dickson in Negri Sembilan and Melaka.
[[nid:1568334]]
He added that about 25 per cent of visitors travelling from Johor to Batam used ferry services, reflecting strong two-way travel demand.
Sigit said expanding ferry services and restoring direct flights between Johor and Indonesian cities would further boost tourism in both countries.
He cited Bandung, Yogyakarta and Lombok as destinations that had more frequent direct flight connections with Johor before the Covid-19 pandemic.
However, flight services had become less frequent following the pandemic, partly due to rising fuel prices and operational challenges.
He said he understood that discussions were under way on the possibility of reinstating a direct flight connection between Bandung and Johor.
"Having more connectivity between Johor Baru and Indonesia will benefit the tourism sector of both countries. Indonesia is also seeing a lot of international tourist arrivals from Malaysia," he said.
The new B Ferry route is part of efforts to strengthen Johor-Batam tourism ties while creating opportunities for local businesses, tourism operators and communities on both sides.
Earlier, Kota Iskandar assemblyman Datuk Pandak Ahmad welcomed the first ferry passengers arriving from Batam at Puteri Harbour International Ferry Terminal.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Rubio flags challenges in finding consensus as G20 talks wrap
Article:
ATLANTA: The United States on Saturday urged against using food trade as a tool for "economic or political coercion," while acknowledging the difficulty of reaching a G20 consensus as foreign ministers wrapped talks.
The US comments sum up a two-day meeting in Atlanta, Georgia, that has been complicated by wars in Iran and Ukraine.
"We are aligned at least in our goal and our understanding that it's a serious problem, although I cannot say we are aligned on how to solve it," said US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who hosted the gathering.
He referred to the rise of food security problems as a result of energy, fertiliser and agricultural products being unable to reach their destinations as sea lanes come under attack.
This comes against the backdrop of the Russia-Ukraine war and follows Iran's retaliation for US and Israeli strikes earlier this year.
"It is important the global community agree that trade in food and agricultural products should not be used as a tool for economic or political coercion," said a chair statement released Saturday by the US G20 presidency.
The talks among the Group of 20 major economies – which includes China, France, Germany, India, Japan and Russia – also took place days before US midterm elections, in which high energy prices are a key voter concern.
It is the last high-level meeting before a G20 leaders' summit in Miami at President Donald Trump's Doral resort in mid-December.
G20 partners now have "some universal acknowledgement" that issues like freedom of navigation matter, alongside supply chains for critical minerals and food security, Rubio told reporters on Saturday.
But he conceded that solving these problems will require much work, with the situation challenged by the Iran and Ukraine wars.
The US chair statement also stressed the need for "secure, resilient, and uninterrupted energy flows, including safe navigation" through waterways.
World energy prices have rocketed since Teheran blocked the Strait of Hormuz – a key waterway for oil transit – in retaliation against US-Israel strikes.
While the potential for further escalation in the Middle East continues to loom, Rubio told a press conference that Trump "hasn't made a decision" on fresh strikes.
At the G20 meeting, European officials also sought to put more pressure on Moscow, particularly to secure a ceasefire in the Black Sea, a key agricultural export corridor.
Asked about the possibility of a ceasefire, Rubio told reporters that there was growing interest internationally to work towards an agreement.
"We'd like to achieve it. It doesn't solve the war, but at least it solves a unique aspect of it," he added.
The US-hosted foreign ministers' meetings closed Saturday with some "sports diplomacy" away from the press.
Ministers were invited to attend an American football game between the University of Georgia and the University of Florida – for which Rubio's son plays.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Couple arrested with 3.2kg of MDMA labelled 'Pink Panther', 'Captain America'
Article:
JASIN: A married couple suspected of acting as drug couriers for an interstate trafficking syndicate were arrested with more than 3.2kg of MDMA in a vehicle along the Alor Gajah-Melaka Tengah-Jasin (AMJ) Highway near Merlimau on Friday.
District police chief Superintendent Lee Robert said the 45-year-old man and 32-year-old woman were detained at 1.30pm by Melaka police contingent headquarters' Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department (NCID), with assistance from the Jasin police headquarters' Crime Prevention and Community Safety Department.
He said a search of the Toyota Vellfire they were travelling in uncovered packets of drugs inside a box on the passenger seat.
"Police also seized the Toyota Vellfire, estimated to be worth RM100,000, 26g of jewellery valued at RM18,814 and RM2,800 in cash, bringing the total value of the seizure to RM617,714.
"The powdered drugs were packed in packets bearing various labels, including 'Pink Panther' and 'Captain America', believed to be intended to mislead the authorities," he said at a press conference at the Jasin police headquarters today.
Lee said the male suspect worked as a cook while the woman was a cashier. Both were from Muar, Johor, and were believed to have been involved in drug collection and handling activities since October.
He said the syndicate had allegedly used the couple as intermediaries to deliver drug supplies around Melaka.
"Investigations are ongoing to identify the source of the drugs, their intended destinations and distribution network, as well as possible involvement of other individuals," he said.
The seized drugs were estimated to be sufficient for 11,096 users.
Lee said preliminary urine screening found both suspects negative for drugs. Neither had any previous criminal or drug-related records.
The couple have been remanded for six days from Oct 31 to Nov 5 to assist investigations under Section 39B of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952, which carries the death penalty or life imprisonment and, if the death penalty is not imposed, at least 12 strokes of the rotan upon conviction.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Guar Chempedak rep, son hurt as SUV overturns in Ulu Sedaka
Article:
YAN: Guar Chempedak assemblyman Abdul Ghafar Saad and his son suffered minor injuries when the Proton X50 sports utility vehicle (SUV) they were travelling in overturned at Ulu Sedaka here yesterday.
The incident was shared in a Facebook post by 'Kaki Jalan 66's', whose members were travelling to the district to take part in the 'Explore Ride Yan Kedah' programme.
According to the post, Ghafar was supposed to join the group for breakfast at a roti canai stall at the location.
"The entire GG Bikers community prays for Ghafar and his son to recover soon and for their affairs to be made easier," the post said.
Meanwhile, Yan deputy police chief Deputy Superintendent Aikap Dunding said in a statement that police received information from a complainant at 8.41am yesterday about an accident involving two vehicles in front of SK Ulu Sedaka.
"Mobile patrol vehicle (MPV) personnel reported that the accident involved the 32-year-old son of the Guar Chempedak assemblyman, who was driving the Proton X50.
"The Guar Chempedak assemblyman was a passenger in the vehicle. He, his son and the driver of the Perodua Myvi sustained minor injuries," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Campaign ‘flag war’ begins in Melaka as parties stretch limited election budgets
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 1 — The excitement surrounding the 16th Melaka State Election is beginning to build, with a “flag war” among political parties visible along roadsides and in public hotspots following the completion of the nomination process yesterday.
A Bernama survey today found that political party flags had been put up in urban areas such as Kota Laksamana, Banda Hilir, Semabok, Duyong, Bukit Katil and Ayer Molek, featuring flags of Pakatan Harapan (PH), Barisan Nasional (BN), Perikatan Nasional (PN), Parti Bersama Malaysia (Bersama) and Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (Bersatu).
Several political parties are reusing flags from previous state elections in Johor and Negeri Sembilan for the Melaka polls.
Political party flags line the roads in Tanjung Bidara, Alor Gajah, ahead of the 16th Melaka state election on October 31, 2026. — Bernama pic
Melaka DAP chairman Khoo Poay Tiong said most of the flags were still in good condition, making their reuse a cost-saving measure to reduce expenses for the Melaka state election.
“We do not have a lot of financial resources, but putting up campaign materials such as flags, posters and banners is important to inform voters in a particular area that PH is contesting there.
“These campaign materials are also intended to introduce to voters the candidates representing PH… the main purpose is to convey that message, rather than compete over who puts up the most flags,” he told Bernama today.
Political party flags are being put up along roads in Tanjung Bidara, Alor Gajah, ahead of the 16th Melaka state election on October 31, 2026. — Bernama pic
He said the installation of PH flags, particularly in areas contested by DAP, was being carried out in stages, especially at locations frequented by the public.
He said about 2,000 flags would be put up in each state constituency contested by the party, with the number to be increased if necessary.
“We will also put up billboards and buntings. We started after the nomination process ended yesterday, and the work is still ongoing. The installation of billboards and buntings will be based on polling district areas and according to need,” he said.
Meanwhile, BN candidate for the Duyong state seat Datuk Mohd Noor Helmy Abdul Halem said the flags displayed around the constituency had also been obtained from friends in Negeri Sembilan and Johor, where the respective state elections had concluded.
“Since Melaka is the third state to hold a state election, we are using whatever flags are available, as our budget is not large,” he said.
He said the installation of flags in the Duyong constituency was still being carried out in stages and was expected to be completed within the next two or three days.
A total of 79 candidates will contest 28 state seats in the 16th Melaka state election following the close of nominations yesterday.
Early voting is scheduled for November 10, while polling day will be held on November 14.
For the latest news on the 16th Melaka state election, visit the Bernama Melaka State Election Portal. — Bernama

Title: Fahmi: Three more Asean countries keen to join Malaysia-led children’s online safety push
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 1 — Thailand, Brunei and Cambodia are the latest Asean countries to have expressed interest in joining Malaysia, Indonesia and Singapore in efforts to address online safety issues involving children.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said he welcomed the development, describing it as a sign that Asean was moving in the same direction.
“In discussions with my counterparts from Indonesia and Singapore, we were already on the same page on this matter. So, this is even better as Southeast Asia will now move in the same direction because we will be stronger when we stand united, especially in dealing with major social media platforms.
“We believe this will help considerably, particularly as these platforms view the region as a single market. So, if the entire or majority of the Southeast Asian market starts speaking about the same issues, then it will be easier,” he said.
Fahmi was speaking at a press conference after attending the Safe Internet Campaign Programme at Multimedia University (MMU), Melaka Campus in Bukit Beruang here today.
Also present was Communications Ministry secretary-general Datuk Abdul Halim Hamzah.
Elaborating on the joint efforts to address children’s online safety issues, Fahmi said Malaysia was also drawing lessons from the way certain restrictions had been implemented in other countries, such as Australia.
“We are also following and taking note of several recent cases in the US, in New Mexico, and this is very helpful in enabling us to take action or plan our next steps,” he said.
Fahmi was previously reported as saying that Malaysia and Indonesia had agreed to establish inter-agency cooperation at the implementation level to address children’s online safety issues, with plans also underway to involve Singapore.
On the Safe Internet Campaign, Fahmi said the programme had so far reached schools throughout Malaysia, with the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) continuing to enhance its content from time to time. — Bernama

Title: BN banks on five-year track record to win fence-sitters at Melaka polls
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 1 — Barisan Nasional (BN) is confident that the achievements and performance of the state administration over the past five years will be among the key factors considered by fence-sitters in determining their choice of candidate in the Melaka state election on November 14.
Melaka BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ab Rauf Yusoh said these voters would assess the party based on its ability to administer the state, as well as the effectiveness of policies and initiatives that directly benefit the people.
“Fence-sitters look at the direction of a party that will be given the mandate to administer a state or country.
“So they will look at what we have delivered to the people while administering the state before making their choice,” he told reporters after inspecting the preparations of the BN election machinery at the Telok Mas state constituency operations room here today.
Ab Rauf, who is also Chief Minister, said approaches taken by the state government to win over the group included the Wakil Rakyat Untuk Rakyat (WRUR), Hari Exco Bertemu Rakyat and Jelajah Ketua Menteri Sayang Rakyat programmes, which focus on identifying and resolving various issues faced by the people.
He said the implementation of the initiatives demonstrated the state government’s commitment to ensuring that every plan and policy was translated into action that benefits the community.
Ab Rauf said that through the WRUR programme, the state government had resolved about 75 per cent of the 4,800 complaints received involving various needs and issues faced by the community.
He said the achievement was among the results of efforts undertaken well before the election.
“We have done the work early so that the people are not sweet-talked during the 14-day campaign period. This is important because we must regard our position as elected representatives... as an opportunity to serve the people, not for the people to serve us,” he said.
Ab Rauf said among the elements frequently assessed by fence-sitters was the ability of each candidate elected as a people’s representative to understand the pulse of the community, including listening to and identifying their problems and needs.
“First, a people’s representative must be one of the people before becoming their representative. They must know the people’s problems, know their needs, listen to what they say and convey it to me so that I can formulate policies that the government can implement in the future,” he said.
Ab Rauf said BN left it to the people to assess all the efforts undertaken by the state government before deciding on their mandate on polling day.
“I hope what we have done and what we have delivered will be the best measure for them to continue working together with us in managing Melaka,” he said.
The Election Commission has set November 14 as polling day for the Melaka polls, while early voting will be held on November 10.
For the latest news on the 16th Melaka State Election, visit https://election.bernama.com/prn/melaka/2026/. — Bernama

Title: Melaka polls: MCMC won’t interfere in parties’ social media campaigns, will only act on complaints
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 1 — The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) will not interfere in social media campaigns by contesting political parties during the 16th Melaka State Election, says Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil.
Instead, he said the commission will actively monitor social media platforms and only initiate investigations or take action against posts upon receiving complaints from the public.
“To date, these are the only two mechanisms MCMC will apply to posts concerning campaigning by contesting parties on social media platforms,” he said when asked about MCMC’s online monitoring measures during the Melaka polls scheduled for November 14.
Fahmi said this at a press conference after attending the Safe Internet Programme at the Multimedia University (MMU) Melaka Campus in Bukit Beruang here today.
