Elaborating, Fahmi said MCMC is also monitoring the misuse of social media accounts to spread false information, the use of deepfakes, and extremely offensive content.
“We are also tracking a trend where content is uploaded by fake accounts, which then disappear once the post is published. This happens frequently and is not something we only anticipate during the state election; it is being detected more often and is quite worrying.
“We found that much of the content containing derogatory statements against the King originated from overseas-based accounts. Upon closer examination, we found that most of them, or 98 per cent, were fake accounts, so we take this very seriously,” he said.
Asked about Pakatan Harapan’s (PH) decision to name Parti Amanah Negara vice-president Adly Zahari as its Chief Minister candidate, Fahmi said it was due to his experience.
“He is an experienced figure. He has served as a state assemblyman for two terms and was previously Chief Minister,” said Fahmi, who is also PH communications director.
PH election director Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari was previously reported as saying that Adly, who is the coalition’s candidate for the Bukit Katil state constituency, was chosen as the poster boy and Chief Minister candidate should the coalition win the Melaka polls.
The Election Commission (EC) has set November 14 as polling day for the 16th Melaka State Election, with early voting on November 10.
For the latest news on the election, visit [https://election.bernama.com/prn/melaka/2026/](https://election.bernama.com/prn/melaka/2026/?utm_source=chatgpt.com). — Bernama

Title: Anwar among racing buffs in Sepang to watch Marquez win Malaysian MotoGP
Article:
SEPANG, Nov 1 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today spent time watching the 2026 Malaysian Motorcycle Grand Prix (GP) race at the Sepang International Circuit (SIC) here.
Anwar’s arrival was welcomed by Minister of Youth and Sports Dr. Mohammed Taufiq Johari and SIC Chief Executive Officer Azhan Shafriman Hanif.
He was then brought to tour the K2 Hillstand spectator seating area before heading to the starting grid to mingle with spectators ahead of the MotoGP class race, which began at 3pm.
The atmosphere at the racing circuit was further enlightened by a rendition of the national anthem, Negaraku, by National Songstress Datuk Seri Siti Nurhaliza Tarudin.
Today’s race saw Ducati Lenovo Team rider Marc Marquez strengthen his position at the summit of the 2026 MotoGP world championship after emerging as the champion, followed by Pedro Acosta of Red Bull KTM Factory Racing in second place and Alex Marquez of BK8 Gresini Racing MotoGP in third.
The victory saw Marc Marquez collect 399 points, thereby widening the gap to 44 points over his closest challenger, Jorge Martin of Aprilia Racing, who now has 355 points. — Bernama

Title: Azalina: All 218 MPs get a role in reforms under CSA as AG-PP split, PM term limit need cross-party support
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 1 — Cross-party cooperation through the Confidence and Supply Agreement (CSA) is important in building parliamentary consensus to advance institutional reforms in the country, said Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said.
In this regard, she welcomed Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi’s support for the implementation of the CSA, as well as his proposal to extend the cooperation to more opposition parties.
She said political differences should not be an obstacle to cooperation for the sake of national stability and the interests of the people, adding that the approach would also provide an avenue for all the existing 218 MPs to play a role in the parliamentary democratic process.
“This is to ensure that the voices of the people represented by their respective Members of Parliament are also involved in determining the direction and future of national institutions through debates and voting in Parliament,” she said in a Facebook post today.
Azalina said the reforms include separating the roles of the Attorney General and the Public Prosecutor, as well as a proposal to limit the Prime Minister’s tenure to 10 years, which require cross-party scrutiny and support as they involve the national interest and amendments to the Federal Constitution.
She said a similar approach to cooperation had previously been implemented when Umno was part of the federal government during the previous term.
Azalina said that as part of the Unity Government, Barisan Nasional (BN) would continue to play a constructive role in maintaining political stability, strengthening democratic institutions and ensuring the country’s administration functions effectively in the interests of the people.
Yesterday, Ahmad Zahid, who is also BN chairman, described the CSA as a positive development in addressing and resolving issues affecting the people.
Last Thursday, the Madani Government signed a CSA with six Bersatu MPs led by its president Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin, as well as seven other MPs, including Muar MP Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman.
On the same day, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said that the agreement was aimed at ensuring the continuity of the government’s administration and the effective implementation of the country’s development agenda, including Budget 2027, in the interests of the people. — Bernama

Title: Zahid: Rural and Regional Development Ministry aims to clear RM259.5m in project arrears by year-end
Article:
BAGAN DATUK, Nov 1 — Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi hopes that outstanding payments for projects under the Rural and Regional Development Ministry (KKDW) can be resolved amicably by the end of this year.
Ahmad Zahid, who is also Rural and Regional Development Minister, said efforts would be made to ensure payments for completed projects that had yet to be settled, including progress payments due to contractors and suppliers, could be made.
“We will endeavour to ensure that funds are made available to settle payments for projects that have been completed but remain unpaid, as well as progress payments due to contractors and suppliers.
“I have explained this matter in Parliament, and it was also answered by the Finance Minister II.
“I hope it can be resolved amicably,” he told a press conference after attending the 2026 Deepavali Santunan Kasih event at the Bagan Datuk Umno Hall here today.
Ahmad Zahid was asked to comment on a video uploaded on TikTok by his press secretary Fadzmel Fadzil, concerning allegations of delayed payments for projects amounting to more than RM200 million.
On October 30, it was reported that outstanding interim payments to contractors and compensation to landowners totalled about RM259.5 million as at September 30, involving 112 projects. — Bernama

Title: BN ready to invite Perikatan to join state govt if it wins Melaka polls, says Zahid
Article:
BAGAN DATUK, Nov 1 — Barisan Nasional (BN) is prepared to invite Perikatan Nasional (PN) to join the state administration if the coalition succeeds in forming the government in the 16th Melaka State Election on November 14.
BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the approach was taken to respect the people’s mandate and the political understanding reached between the two coalitions, similar to what had previously been implemented in Negeri Sembilan.
“As happened in Negeri Sembilan, when the government was formed, we honoured the appointments to ensure that they (PN) were part of the government. The same happened in Melaka when the previous Unity Government was formed, with our partners in PH (Pakatan Harapan) also appointed as state executive councillors (Exco) and deputy Exco members, but they subsequently decided to leave.
“So we will do the same for PN assemblymen who win their respective seats and, God willing, if we form the government, we will also invite them to be part of the state government,” he told a press conference after attending the 2026 Deepavali Santunan Kasih event at Dewan Umno Bagan Datuk here today.
In this election, BN is contesting 23 of the 28 seats up for grabs, while PN is contesting five seats.
The Election Commission has set November 14 as polling day for the Melaka state election, while early voting will take place on November 10.
For the latest news on the 16th Melaka state election, visit
https://election.bernama.com/prn/melaka/2026
. — Bernama

Title: Four dead as cars veer into oncoming lanes in separate KL, Johor crashes
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 1 — Four people were killed in two separate road accidents involving four vehicles in Kuala Lumpur and Kulai, Johor, with both crashes believed to have occurred after cars veered into oncoming lanes.
In an accident involving a Perodua Myvi and a Toyota Vellfire at Kilometer 23 of the Middle Ring Road 2 (MRR2), near Bukit Antarabangsa, early this morning, two men were killed.
Ampang Jaya district police Chief ACP Khairul Anuar Khalid said in the 12.40am incident, the Myvi, which was travelling from Taman Melawati towards Cheras, is believed to have lost control before skidding into the opposite lane.
He said the vehicle then collided with the front of the Vellfire travelling in the opposite direction.
“The Myvi driver sustained serious head injuries and was pronounced dead at the scene by medical personnel from Ampang Hospital,” he said in a statement today.
He said the Vellfire driver and a passenger were also injured and rushed to Ampang Hospital; however, the driver was pronounced dead while receiving treatment at the hospital, while the passenger remains hospitalised.
Khairul Anuar said the case is being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.
He urged witnesses to come forward to assist in the investigation by contacting the Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Division at the Ampang Jaya district police headquarters.
A video showing the aftermath of the accident had earlier gone viral on social media.
Meanwhile, in Kulai, a mother and her daughter were killed in an accident involving two vehicles at Jalan Senai-Lapangan Terbang Antarabangsa Senai here yesterday.
Kulai district police chief ACP Tan Seng Lee said police received information about the accident involving a Toyota Vios and a Mazda at about 2.30pm.
He said the accident is believed to have occurred when the Mazda, driven by a 30-year-old woman with her 69-year-old mother as a passenger, skidded into the opposite lane.
“The accident left the Mazda driver seriously injured. She was pronounced dead while receiving treatment at Temenggong Seri Maharaja Tun Ibrahim Hospital, while her mother died at Sultanah Aminah Hospital.
“However, the 30-year-old male driver of the Toyota Vios sustained only minor injuries. The actual cause of the accident is still under investigation,” he said in a statement today.
Tan said the case is being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.
Members of the public with information about the accident can contact the Kulai district police headquarters Traffic Division or the investigating officer, Inspector Ahmad Safuan Abu Naim, at 017-7573507 to assist the investigation. — Bernama

Title: Sarawak explores collaboration with Russia on rocket, satellite launches, says Abang Johari
Article:
KUCHING, Nov 1 — The Sarawak government is exploring potential collaboration with Russia in rocket and satellite launches, leveraging the state’s strategic location near the Equator.
Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Openg said the proposal was raised by the Ambassador of the Russian Federation to Malaysia, Naiyl M. Latypov, during a courtesy call last week.
“I mentioned that we (Sarawak) require more engineers and are prepared to explore collaboration to develop a larger pool of professionals in the field,” he said at the inauguration of the extension building of Gurdwara Sahib Kuching here today.
Abang Johari said Sarawak must capitalise on growing international interest in the state by implementing effective policies and ensuring clear development plans.
Recently, local media reported that Russia had expressed its readiness to discuss potential collaboration with Sarawak in various sectors, including aerospace, energy, agriculture, shipbuilding and education. — Bernama

Title: AGC files appeal, weighs bid to reinstate murder charge against senior Perak cop in student hit-and-run case
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Nov 1 — The Attorney General’s Chambers (AGC) is considering whether to seek the reinstatement of a murder charge against a senior police officer in the case involving the death of student Muhammad Zaharif Affendi Muhd Zamrie, following the officer’s conviction on a lesser charge of causing death.
Attorney General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar said the AGC had filed an appeal at the Court of Appeal last week against the Ipoh High Court’s decision, but was still examining the various aspects of the case before deciding on the arguments to be submitted.
He said he had discussed the matter with AGC Prosecution Division head Datuk Masri Mohd Daud and the head of its Trial and Appeals Division.
“We want to examine every aspect of this case, including whether we should submit arguments for the original murder charge to be reinstated, or take any other appropriate action based on the circumstances of the case and the court’s decision,” he said.
Mohd Dusuki was speaking to reporters after attending the launch of the Attorney-General’s Chambers Madani Adopted School programme at Sekolah Kebangsaan Pasir Hor here today.
Asked whether the AGC had identified any gaps or shortcomings in the High Court’s decision, Mohd Dusuki said it was too early to comment as the prosecution had yet to receive the full grounds of judgment.
On October 28, the Ipoh High Court sentenced DSP Mohd Nazri Abdul Razak, 47, to seven years and six months’ imprisonment after he pleaded guilty to an amended charge of causing the death of Muhammad Zaharif, three years ago.
The charge was amended from murder under Section 302 of the Penal Code to one under Section 304(b), which carries a maximum jail term of 10 years, a fine, or both, upon conviction.
The judge ordered Mohd Nazri to serve his sentence from December 15, 2023, the date of his arrest. He was also ordered to pay RM50,000 in compensation to the victim’s father, Muhd Zamrie Zainal Abidin, 58, or face an additional year in prison if he failed to do so.
Mohd Nazri was accused of causing the death of Muhammad Zaharif, 17, near Sekolah Menengah Kebangsaan Jati in Ipoh between 11.55am and 12.32pm on December 15, 2023.
He was initially charged under Section 302 of the Penal Code, which carries the death penalty or imprisonment of between 30 and 40 years and at least 12 strokes of the cane upon conviction. — Bernama

Title: Brace for the toughest GE yet: Loke warns DAP as BN and Perikatan close ranks
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 1 — DAP must prepare for its toughest general election yet as growing cooperation between Barisan Nasional (BN) and Perikatan Nasional (PN) threatens to upend the country’s political landscape, Anthony Loke said today.
The DAP secretary-general warned that recent political pacts struck between the two coalitions across Johor, Negeri Sembilan, and Melaka present a serious challenge to DAP and its Pakatan Harapan (PH) partners, NST reported.
Addressing delegates at the Kuala Lumpur Federal Territories DAP annual convention today, Loke urged members to cast aside complacency and tighten the party’s machinery ahead of the 16th general election (GE16).
“Whatever their political calculations, the most important thing is that our party must remain united and strengthen ourselves together with our partners in Pakatan Harapan,” he said.
With the convention likely serving as the party’s final annual gathering in the capital before GE16, Loke called on members to ramp up ground preparations and prioritise defending their parliamentary seats. DAP’s core objective in Kuala Lumpur remains retaining all five parliamentary seats secured during the 15th general election (GE15).
“Kuala Lumpur DAP must help the party defend all five seats that we won in GE15,” he said. PH currently holds 10 of the 11 parliamentary seats across the Federal Territories.
Loke stressed that public support can no longer be taken for granted, citing the party’s recent electoral drubbings as a critical wake-up call.
DAP reassessed its ground strategy after a devastating wipeout in the November 2025 Sabah state election, where it lost all eight contested seats, including six traditional strongholds.
State poll wake-up calls
The electoral tremors continued into earlier state contests. In the July Johor election, DAP secured only six of the 17 seats it contested, surrendering four previously held constituencies.
In August, the party took nine of 11 seats in Negeri Sembilan, but suffered a high-profile casualty when Loke himself lost the Chennah state seat to MCA’s Siow Kong Choon by 688 votes.
Loke confirmed that DAP conducted an extensive post-mortem to address systemic weaknesses uncovered during those defeats, noting that those hard lessons must dictate future campaign strategy.
“The challenges we face are becoming greater as we approach the next election,” he warned.
Beyond the ballot box, Loke acknowledged that party leaders have become frequent targets of political attacks and viral satire online.
While accepting that criticism comes with the territory of holding federal power, he insisted members must stay focused on public delivery rather than retreating into defensiveness.
Acknowledging federal administrative shortcomings, Loke urged leaders to proactively communicate the coalition’s tangible reforms to the electorate.
He noted that doing the right thing does not always bring immediate political dividends, but leaders cannot abandon their core duties under the weight of electoral pressure.

Title: Immigration Dept: Report special pass irregularities directly to us or MACC
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Nov 1 — The Immigration Department (JIM) has urged the public to report alleged irregularities in the issuance of Special Passes involving its officers in Kuala Lumpur directly to the authorities.
Immigration director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said information or evidence could be submitted to JIM or the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) to facilitate a comprehensive investigation.
“Providing information directly to the authorities is crucial to protecting the confidentiality of information and preserving the integrity of evidence.
“Publicly disclosing information about suspected unlawful activities before reporting it to the authorities could prompt those involved to halt their activities, change their modus operandi or destroy evidence, thereby hindering investigations and enforcement action,” he said in a statement today.
Zakaria said JIM welcomed information on alleged misconduct by its officers and would ensure that all reports received were reviewed and referred for appropriate action under the prevailing laws and regulations.
He said the department viewed the allegations seriously and would not tolerate misconduct, abuse of power or breaches of integrity by its officers, regardless of rank or position.
As part of efforts to strengthen integrity and accountability, Zakaria said a total of 849 immigration officers had faced disciplinary action from 2023 to October this year, including 73 who were dismissed.
From January to October this year alone, 96 officers faced disciplinary action, including 18 who were dismissed.
He said the figures reflected the department’s firm stance on taking action against officers found to have committed disciplinary offences.
JIM would continue to strengthen integrity, procedural compliance and internal controls to ensure that all services were delivered transparently and in accordance with the law, he added. — Bernama

Title: Anwar: Manage govt funds with care or face arrest, charges
Article:
KAJANG, Nov 1 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today stressed that government funds must be properly safeguarded and managed, warning that strict action would be taken against anyone who betrayed the trust placed in them.
Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, said agencies providing financing for entrepreneurship, including the National Entrepreneurial Group Economic Fund (TEKUN Nasional), Bank Rakyat and Amanah Ikhtiar Malaysia (AIM), bore a major responsibility to ensure funds reached their intended beneficiaries without leakage or misappropriation.
“Manage these funds properly... This is money held in trust. If you breach that trust, you will be arrested and charged. Only then can we safeguard our country,” he said.
He was speaking at the closing ceremony of the 2026 National Hawkers and Small Traders Day (HPPK) Carnival here, which was also attended by Entrepreneur Development and Cooperatives Minister Steven Sim and Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek.
Also present were Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari, Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar and Malaysian Malay Hawkers and Small Traders Associations Federation (GPPPKMM) president Datuk Zainal Abidin Abd Majid.
On the country’s fiscal capacity, Anwar said the Madani Government’s efficient and transparent governance has enabled it to increase various forms of assistance and allocations for the people.
He said welfare allocations, including the Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) and Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA) aid, which will total RM16 billion next year, as well as the RM18 billion allocation for civil servants’ salary adjustments implemented this year, were made possible by the government’s improved management of public finances.
“Some people question how we can afford to increase allocations. It is because there is no leakage, no misappropriation, and no corruption. Insya-Allah, there are blessings in this, and we are helping the people. That is our purpose,” he said.
Anwar also stressed that the Madani Government remained committed to addressing the concerns of people nationwide, including in opposition-governed states, dismissing allegations that the government practised discrimination.
He said the government was committed to resolving the people’s problems regardless of political affiliation, including reinstating special assistance for religious teachers and repairing dilapidated pondok school buildings that had been neglected since 2003.
“Kelantan is governed by a different political party, but the people’s problems are our problems too. This is different from what we hear about alleged discrimination, that we do not provide assistance or that the Malays are not receiving anything.
“When we took over in 2022, we felt that this was not a fair system. We said we wanted to look after the people, so we assisted,” he said.
Anwar urged all parties not to defend abuses of power and corruption, but instead to collectively uphold values of decency, morality and integrity for the country’s prosperity.
“We are called upon to uphold what is good and reject what is wrong,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia ranked 12th of 163 in 2026 Global Peace Index, reflecting security efforts, says Saifuddin Nasution
Article:
RAUB, Nov 1 — Malaysia’s 12th-place ranking among 163 countries in the 2026 Global Peace Index (GPI) reflects the country’s ongoing efforts to maintain safety and security, particularly through the work of the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM), said Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail.
He said the ranking reflected a secure environment that allowed Malaysians to go about their daily lives in peace and comfort, without undue concern over security threats.
“To maintain this achievement, the government has also established the Independent Police Conduct Commission (IPCC) to further improve the quality of police services.
Our target is to move Malaysia up from 12th to ninth place, with the aim of achieving an even better ranking in the future,” he said at the IPCC’s Santuni Madani programme in Kampung Kela here today.
Saifuddin Nasution said the IPCC played an important role in ensuring that the police force continued to uphold high standards in carrying out its duties.
“Our target is to move Malaysia up from 12th to ninth place, with the aim of achieving an even better ranking in the future,” he said at the IPCC’s Santuni Madani programme in Kampung Kela here today.
Saifuddin Nasution said the IPCC played an important role in ensuring that the police force continued to uphold high standards in carrying out its duties.
“A commission such as this is vital, and in many other countries, similar bodies hold a strong and significant position,” he added.
At the programme, the Home Ministry (KDN), through the IPCC, distributed essential goods and equipment worth RM20,000 to five surau (small prayer halls) and eight families with members who have permanent disabilities in the village.
In a statement, the IPCC said the Santuni Madani programme was part of its efforts to strengthen ties between its leadership and local communities under the One Leader, One Village initiative.
The programme provided an opportunity for direct engagement with residents to better understand their needs and facilitate access to government services, particularly those under the purview of KDN, the statement said.
It also served as a platform to raise public awareness of the IPCC’s functions and role, including among the Orang Asli community.
The IPCC said the participation of various agencies under KDN underscored the importance of an inclusive approach to improving public access to information and government services. — Bernama

Title: Foster healthy lifestyles: Nearly two million Malaysians benefit from 38 Wellness Hubs nationwide, says Dzulkefly
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 1 — Nearly two million people have benefited from 38 Wellness Hub facilities operating nationwide under the Ministry of Health’s (MOH) initiative to expand access to disease prevention and foster healthy lifestyles.
Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said two of these facilities are located in Melaka, namely in Alor Gajah and Melaka Tengah, serving as community wellness referral centres.
He said the initiative is part of the ministry’s drive to shift the national healthcare model from solely treating illnesses to preventive care, particularly in addressing the rise of non-communicable diseases (NCDs).
“These are not clinics or hospitals for the sick; they are one-stop centres for people who want to stay healthy. At Wellness Hubs, we offer weight management services (IFitEr), smoking cessation support, mental health screenings, the ‘Stay Active’ module, and exercise therapy,” he said.
He told a press conference after officiating the national-level Wellness Month (BMSS) 2026 celebration in Ayer Keroh here today.
Dzulkefly said the preventive approach adopted by Wellness Hubs has shown promising results, with 87 per cent, or 460 of the 528 participants in its weight management pilot programme, successfully losing weight.
“Another 438 participants, or 83 per cent, improved their physical fitness, while 111 achieved a normal body mass index (BMI). This proves that with guidance, people can change,” he said.
He stressed that strengthening preventive healthcare has become increasingly critical due to the rise in NCDs, which he described as a silent pandemic costing the national economy up to RM64.2 billion a year.
Of that amount, RM51.8 billion, or 80.69 per cent, stems from lost productivity, while RM12.4 billion covers treatment costs.
Although public health literacy has improved through the National Agenda for a Healthy Malaysia (ANMS), Dzulkefly noted that the primary challenge remains translating knowledge into daily behavioural change.
To address this, he said the ministry has adopted a behavioural ‘nudging’ approach by creating supportive environments and facilities that encourage healthier choices, involving stakeholders including community leaders, Members of Parliament, and state assemblymen.
“If we want to shift from sick care to healthcare, we cannot simply ask people to stay healthy without providing the necessary facilities or environment.
“This is crucial because the strength of a healthcare system is measured not only by its capacity to treat patients in hospitals, but also by its ability to help people stay healthy so they do not require treatment,” he said.
Meanwhile, Dzulkefly said RM3.381 million had been spent on applications under the Malaysian Community Health Agent (MyCHAMPION) programme between 2025 and October this year to empower community participation in national health initiatives. — Bernama

Title: Zahid: Govt on alert, ramps up readiness as El Nino raises monsoon flood risks
Article:
BAGAN DATUK, Nov 1 — The government and all relevant agencies are fully prepared to face the North-east Monsoon (MTL), which is expected to have a more severe impact than in previous years.
Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the state of preparedness involved comprehensive coordination between the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma) and disaster management committees at state and district levels, following the launch of National Preparedness Month 2026 in Ipoh last month.
“This year’s North-east Monsoon is expected to have a more severe impact than in previous years, following an El Nino episode that affected many countries, particularly in Asean.
“Nadma, in collaboration with all enforcement agencies, has identified hotspots where unusually heavy rainfall is expected,” he told a press conference after attending the ‘2026 Deepavali Santunan Kasih’ event at the Bagan Datuk Umno Hall here today.
Asked whether certain states would be the main focus during the monsoon season, Ahmad Zahid said Kelantan, Terengganu, the northern states, particularly Kedah, as well as southern states comprising Johor, Melaka and Negeri Sembilan were frequently affected by the North-east Monsoon.
Ahmad Zahid, who is also National Disaster Management Committee chairman, said responsibilities had been assigned to rescue agencies, while the Social Welfare Department (JKM) was prepared with stockpiles of food aid and fully equipped evacuation tents, with additional support from non-governmental organisations (NGOs).
On Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) candidates who would be sitting for their examinations during the monsoon season, he assured that the welfare of the students and the smooth conduct of their examinations remained a priority for the government.
He said he had discussed the matter with Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek at a recent Cabinet meeting, with contingency plans being drawn up to accommodate affected students at school hostels.
“She (Fadhlina) informed me that students in areas expected to experience severe flooding had been identified and would be relocated to schools with hostels, where they would sit for their examinations. The Examinations Board is also fully prepared for this,” he said.
Meanwhile, Ahmad Zahid said improvements to the Bantuan Wang Ihsan (BWI) compassionate aid scheme, introduced last year, would continue, with RM1,000 in aid channelled directly to each family while they were at temporary relief centres.
He said the measure would enable flood victims to use the assistance immediately upon returning home to clean their houses and replace damaged household items, provided they had officially relocated to a relief centre, to prevent leakages.
He said flood victims previously had to wait two weeks and visit a bank to collect the assistance, but under the new arrangement, the RM1,000 would be handed to them directly once they were at the relief centres.
“However, those who do not relocate, even if their names are on the list, will not receive the assistance.
“They must move to a relief centre to ensure the funds are not misappropriated or channelled to other parties,” he said.
At the event, Ahmad Zahid also presented Deepavali essential supplies to 2,000 B40 households across the Bagan Datuk parliamentary constituency, as well as RM100 each in year-end educational assistance to 700 pupils from Tamil National-type Schools (SJKT), involving a total allocation of RM70,000.
He also presented Smartboard TVs to all 16 SJKTs in the constituency to support digital learning facilities.
In addition, Ahmad Zahid presented educational assistance of RM3,000 to each of the 12 kindergartens serving the Indian community in Bagan Datuk, involving a total allocation of RM36,000. — Bernama

Title: Adly Zahari to be Pakatan’s chief minister candidate if coalition wins Melaka
Article:
KAJANG, Nov 1 — Deputy Defence Minister Adly Zahari will be named Pakatan Harapan’s (PH) candidate for Chief Minister if the coalition succeeds in forming the state government following the 16th Melaka State Election on November 14.
PH Election director Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said Adly, a former Melaka Chief Minister, was the best candidate for the position.
“Adly is the best candidate (for Chief Minister), along with a few others. However, as of now, there is a consensus to name Adly as the candidate, provided we secure a majority or are entrusted with the mandate,” he told reporters here today.
Amirudin, who is also Selangor Menteri Besar, told reporters this after the closing of the National-Level Hawkers and Small Traders Day Carnival (HPPK) 2026 by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
In the election, Adly, the incumbent Bukit Katil assemblyman, faces a four-cornered contest against Perikatan Nasional (PN) candidate Ridzuan Sarif, Parti Bersama Malaysia (Bersama) candidate Dr Aliza Che Amran, and independent candidate Abu Bakar Sabudin.
In the 15th Melaka State Election, Adly, who is also an Amanah vice-president, won the seat with a majority of 1,057 votes, defeating three other candidates — Datuk Hasnoor Sdg Husin of Barisan Nasional (BN), Muhammad Al Afiz Yahya of PN, and independent candidate Abdul Hamid.
Elaborating, Amirudin, who is also a PKR vice-president, said PH was confident of mounting a strong challenge in the state election following the conclusion of the nomination process yesterday.
The Election Commission has set November 14 as polling day for the 16th Melaka State Election, while early voting is on November 10.
For the latest updates on the 16th Melaka State Election, visit
https://election.bernama.com/prn/melaka/2026/
. — Bernama

Title: Sepang circuit must be more than just a race track: Deputy minister pushes for serious F1 evaluation
Article:
SEPANG, Nov 1 — The possibility of bringing Formula 1 (F1) racing back to Malaysia must be seriously evaluated, while the Sepang International Circuit (SIC) must be strengthened as a strategic national asset, says Deputy Housing and Local Government Minister Aiman Athirah Sabu.
Aiman Athirah, who is also Sepang MP, said this was to ensure that every investment generated economic returns, created job opportunities and brought tangible benefits to the people.
“In this regard, I hope Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim will give due consideration to the future of SIC as a strategic national asset with international value, geographical advantages and huge potential to stimulate economic growth.
“SIC is not merely a racing circuit. It is a strategic national asset, a tourism catalyst, an investment platform and Malaysia’s gateway to remaining competitive in the global motorsports industry,” she said in a statement on her Facebook page today.
Meanwhile, Aiman Athirah said the decision to extend Malaysia’s hosting rights for the MotoGP until 2031 was an important step in maintaining the country’s position on the international motorsports calendar.
She said SIC needed to diversify its revenue streams through corporate sponsorships, commercial rights, hospitality packages, facility rentals, additional events and strategic partnerships with automotive manufacturers and international industry partners.
“I welcome SIC’s efforts to prepare a feasibility study on bringing F1 back to Malaysia, which is reportedly scheduled to be presented to the Cabinet in November.
“However, the decision to bring F1 back must not be based solely on nostalgia, prestige or spectator attendance. It must be guided by a thorough economic study, taking into account hosting fees, operational commitments, sponsorships, commercial revenue and net returns to the country,” she said.
She also proposed that the government consider several hosting models, including annual races if proven financially and commercially viable, or periodic races if such an approach offered a more optimal cost-benefit ratio.
She said SIC should also be developed into a year-round motorsports economic hub rather than relying solely on a few major racing weekends each year to generate revenue.
“Among the areas worth exploring are international motorsports events, vehicle testing and development by automotive manufacturers, technical training programmes, industry conferences, corporate activities and facility rentals for various commercial purposes.
“More importantly, SIC should be given a greater role in developing local talent and the domestic industry through collaborations with universities, Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) institutions and automotive industry players,” she said. — Bernama

Title: Pakatan tells its supporters in Melaka: Vote with your conscience
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 1 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) is taking an open approach and leaving it to its members and supporters to decide whom to support in state seats not contested by the coalition in the 16th Melaka state election.
Melaka PH chairman Adly Zahari said the coalition had never issued any specific directive instructing its members and supporters to support any particular party in those constituencies, expressing confidence that they understood the political dynamics of the current state election.
He said PH’s current focus was on securing victory in the 24 state seats contested by the coalition.
“So, for our supporters in constituencies where PH is not contesting, whom they support is the right of our members. We understand how they should cast their votes in the coming election,” he told reporters at the 2026 national-level Malaysia Sihat Sejahtera Month in Ayer Keroh here today.
Asked about Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia’s (Bersatu) decision to contest eight state seats, Adly said the party had its own plans for the Melaka state election.
“I think Bersatu has its own plans, as it is contesting eight seats. We are focused on PH, and we understand that our main rivals are Barisan Nasional and Perikatan Nasional,” he said.
The Election Commission (EC) has set Nov 14 as polling day for the 16th Melaka state election, with early voting scheduled for Nov 10. — Bernama

Title: Anwar pledges RM1m boost for hawkers and urges an end to tedious loan paperwork
Article:
KAJANG, Nov 1 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has announced an allocation of RM1 million to the Ministry of Entrepreneur Development and Cooperatives (KUSKOP) to coordinate assistance for associations, hawkers, and small traders to boost their income.
He said the allocation takes into account the hundreds of thousands of hawkers, small traders, and associations operating nationwide.
“Initially, I thought of announcing RM100,000, which is already a significant amount, but then I considered that there are hundreds of thousands of hawkers, businesses, stalls, and associations across the country, so let us manage this properly.
“(The government) is providing assistance so that every year we see an increase in the income of hawkers and traders,” he said in his speech at the closing ceremony of the national-level Hawkers and Small Traders Day (HPPK) Carnival 2026 here today.
Also present were Entrepreneur Development and Cooperatives Minister Steven Sim, Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek, Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari, and Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar.
Also in attendance was Federation of Malay Hawkers and Small Traders Associations of Malaysia (GPPPKMM) president Datuk Zainal Abidin Abd Majid.
Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, said the allocation channelled to associations, hawkers, and small traders would help improve family incomes.
“If you ask me whether Anwar is satisfied with the plight of hawkers, I am not satisfied because they make up the majority of the people and their lives are hard. They live hand-to-mouth.
“If we ask them to go to an office and spend a whole day filling in loan forms, that is a burden on them. So we must find ways to increase their income,” he said.
The Prime Minister also asked Steven Sim to work with relevant associations to obtain data on the income growth and average earnings of hawkers and small traders over the past three years.
“This is how we assess our weaknesses and shortcomings, because if we can help hawkers and small traders, it will benefit one million families in our country,” he said.
Meanwhile, Anwar urged hawkers to keep their stalls clean and presentable, noting that about 85 per cent of the population choose to eat at street stalls and food outlets.
“That is why, since becoming Prime Minister four years ago, every week before or after Friday prayers, I have lunch at food stalls to show that we should support these small businesses and traders.
“Sometimes the food is tastier than at large restaurants, but more importantly, it is much cheaper.
“If I want the stalls to be clean and have well-maintained roofs, I believe the public wants the same,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Najib still to pay RM50m fine needed for house arrest, says AG
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Nov 1 — Former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak has yet to pay his RM50 million fine, according to the latest information received by the Attorney-General’s Chambers (AGC).
Attorney-General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar said no specific deadline had been set for payment of the fine.
“So far, the information we have received indicates that Datuk Seri Najib has yet to fulfil the requirement as of now,” he told reporters after attending the launch of the Attorney-General’s Chambers MADANI Adopted School Programme at Sekolah Kebangsaan Pasir Hor here today.
Asked whether Najib would still have to serve his prison sentence as long as the fine remained unpaid, Mohd Dusuki confirmed that this was the case.
On Sept 18, the media reported that His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, had granted Najib a conditional pardon, allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028.
The order was conditional upon Najib paying the RM50 million fine.
The Legal Affairs Division of the Prime Minister’s Department said the decision was made at the 64th Meeting of the Pardons Board for the Federal Territories of Kuala Lumpur, Labuan and Putrajaya, held at Istana Negara.
In July 2020, the Kuala Lumpur High Court sentenced Najib to 12 years’ imprisonment and fined him RM210 million after finding him guilty of misappropriating RM42 million belonging to SRC International Sdn Bhd. The sentence was subsequently upheld by the Court of Appeal in December 2021 and the Federal Court in August 2022.
However, at its 61st meeting on Jan 29, 2024, the Pardons Board decided to reduce the former Pekan MP’s prison sentence from 12 years to six years and the fine from RM210 million to RM50 million.
Meanwhile, on Dec 26 last year, the High Court sentenced the former prime minister to 15 years’ imprisonment and fined him RM11.4 billion after finding him guilty of four charges of abuse of power and 21 charges of money laundering involving RM2.3 billion in 1MDB funds.
He filed an appeal on Dec 29, 2025.
In a civil case, the High Court on March 31 ordered Najib to repay US$1.3 billion to SRC International after finding that he had breached his fiduciary duties, abused his position and misappropriated company funds for personal gain. However, enforcement of the payment order was stayed pending the outcome of his appeal.
Najib is also facing two other lawsuits, one filed by SRC International and another by Gandingan Mentari Sdn Bhd in 2021, as well as a US$5.64 billion civil suit filed by 1MDB and four of its subsidiaries. All remain before the courts. — Bernama

Title: DAP urges government to make Najib’s pardon board minutes public
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 1 — DAP has urged Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim to release the minutes of the Federal Territories Pardons Board (FTPB) meeting regarding former prime minister Najib Razak’s conditional pardon.
DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke said that while the party hopes the minutes will be declassified, it understands that the final decision rests with the attorney-general.
“We have conveyed our request to the prime minister, but there are procedures to declassify the minutes,” Loke said in a
FMT
report.
Speaking earlier at the Federal Territories DAP convention, Loke acknowledged that Najib’s conditional pardon has sparked significant public questioning.
He said Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh, a board member, had clearly communicated the party’s stance against house arrest for those involved in major corruption scandals.
“Someone involved in a major corruption scandal should not be released or granted house arrest,” he maintained.
Najib was imprisoned in August 2022 after the Federal Court upheld convictions for abuse of power, criminal breach of trust, and money laundering involving RM42 million in SRC funds. He received a 12-year sentence and a RM210 million fine.
In January 2024, then Yang diPertuan Agong Al-Sultan Abdullah Sultan Ahmad Shah halved Najib’s jail term and reduced the fine to RM50 million.
Later, in September this year, His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, granted a further conditional pardon allowing Najib to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until 23 August 2028, provided he pays the RM50 million fine and meets other conditions.
Najib has not yet paid the fine, though Umno has launched a crowdfunding campaign to help the former president settle the debt.
Support for Bersatu stability deal
Turning to government stability, Loke confirmed that DAP supports the confidence and supply agreement (CSA) with six Bersatu MPs, noting that the Pakatan Harapan presidential council has endorsed the deal.
He explained that the agreement, formally a memorandum of understanding (MoU), is open to all opposition MPs to ensure political stability without requiring them to formally join the government.
Loke drew a parallel to a similar MoU signed between PH and then prime minister Datuk Seri Ismail Sabri Yaakob in 2021.
“That did not mean we supported Ismail at the time. We simply wanted to prevent attempts to bring down the government,” he clarified.
Loke added that the current agreement aims to prevent a return to the political turmoil of 2020, while reiterating DAP’s demand for the institutionalisation of equal allocations for all MPs.

Title: No registration needed: STR recipients 40 and above automatically qualify for PeKa Sihat, says Teo Nie Ching
Article:
KULAI, Nov 1 — Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) recipients aged 40 and above are urged to make full use of the PeKa Sihat (Healthcare Scheme for the B40 Group) initiative, which offers various free health screenings and treatments starting next year following an RM80 million government allocation.
Deputy Communications Minister Teo Nie Ching said this group and their spouses qualify for the benefits automatically without going through a complicated registration process.
“Checks can be done easily via the official PeKa Sihat website by entering their identity card numbers to verify eligibility and find the list of participating private clinics,” she told reporters after the Bukit Permai state constituency Deepavali contribution presentation ceremony at the Arulmigu Mariamman Temple here today.
She noted that a key benefit of the initiative is free health screenings at private clinics to detect conditions such as diabetes and high cholesterol, thereby easing congestion at government health facilities.
PeKa Sihat also provides medical equipment aid of up to RM20,000, covering items such as heart stents, artificial joints, hearing aids, pacemakers, and intraocular lenses for cataract surgery.
A special RM1,000 incentive for cancer patients to complete their treatment and a hospital transport allowance are also provided.
Administered by ProtectHealth, PeKa Sihat is a government healthcare initiative aimed at encouraging eligible Malaysians to undergo health screenings and identify health risks early.
It was previously reported that as of September 2026, 2.1 million Malaysians had undergone health screenings under the programme.
In 2025, 328,302 individuals were screened under PeKa Sihat, with 44.5 per cent found to have at least one previously undetected health issue.
Meanwhile, touching on today’s programme, Teo said about RM100,000 in aid had been distributed in the Kulai parliamentary constituency in conjunction with this year’s Deepavali celebration through cooperation with temples and welfare associations.
She added that the contribution aims to ease the local community’s financial burden in preparing for the festival. — Bernama

Title: Puchong plant processes 40,000 chickens daily, used stunning voltage up to 13 times halal limit, say police
Article:
PUCHONG, Nov 1 — A chicken processing plant in Kampung Sri Aman Hilir here, raided during Op Taring Chiller, is believed to have the capacity to process more than 40,000 chickens a day, while allegedly using electrical voltage far exceeding the prescribed limit for the slaughtering method.
Bukit Aman Internal Security and Public Order Department (JKDNKA) deputy director (Operations) Datuk Muhammad Abdul Halim said preliminary investigations found that the live chickens were sourced from Sungai Sepat, Sungai Pelek and Sepang before being processed at the plant.
He said the processed chickens were then believed to have been distributed to customers, including eateries, grocery shops and business premises in Damansara, Bangi, Puchong, Cheras, Putra Perdana and Putrajaya.
“Based on the machine’s capacity, the premises can process more than 40,000 chickens a day. However, the actual number processed is still under investigation.
“We are also identifying the entire supply and distribution network, including the premises receiving chicken supplies from the plant,” he told a press conference after inspecting the plant here today.
Commenting on the water-bath stunning method used at the plant, Muhammad said investigations found that the premises had allegedly used electrical voltage exceeding the prescribed limit, resulting in the chickens dying before the slaughtering process.
He said inspections found that a voltage of 60 volts was used at the first gate near the front section, while 130 volts was applied at the second gate in the middle section, whereas the Selangor Islamic Religious Department (JAIS) stipulates that the voltage used for the method must be below 10 volts.
“This is a matter of grave concern as the slaughtering method is one of the key elements in determining the halal status of a chicken product,” he said.
He said the Department of Islamic Development Malaysia (JAKIM) had previously issued several notices and reminders for the plant, which had been operating for more than 10 years, to comply with the prescribed procedures, but it had continued to fail to do so.
During the raid at 12.40am last Friday, police also arrested 12 Bangladeshi men who were found to be without valid travel documents. They have been remanded for 14 days from yesterday until November 13.
The premises’ owner, a local man in his early 30s, also had his statement recorded, while further action will be determined based on the outcome of the investigation, including his role and involvement in the plant’s operations.
Meanwhile, the Department of Environment (DOE) issued a notice to impound the operational equipment at the premises, while the seized chickens were temporarily placed at the Selangor Islamic Religious Department (JAIS) in Shah Alam pending disposal.
The media had earlier reported that more than 6.5 tonnes of raw chicken worth RM85,400 were seized during the integrated operation over suspicions that they had been processed in breach of Islamic slaughtering requirements and halal certification standards.
The case is being investigated under Section 3(1)(A) and Section 4(1) of the Trade Descriptions (Definition of Halal) Order 2011, as well as Section 38(1) of the Environmental Quality Act 1974. — Bernama

Title: Malaysians face pricey Indian onions as fresh supply delays cloud Deepavali festival
Article:
PHNOM PENH, Nov 1 — Malaysian consumers could pay more for Indian onions ahead of the Deepavali festival as production in Maharashtra, India’s biggest producing state, falls nearly 40 per cent due to weak rainfall.
Irregular rainfall and prolonged dry spells this monsoon have delayed the arrival of fresh kharif onions, the monsoon-season crop, adding price pressure to local Indian markets.
“There could be about a 30 to 40 per cent production drop in Maharashtra because of drought. Farmers across India are facing a shortage of rain due to El Niño and this is impacting onion production because of poor moisture. Prices could gradually increase,” Lasalgaon Agricultural Produce Market Committee Chairman Dnyaneshwar Kisan Jagtap told Bernama on Saturday.
Lasalgaon, a town in the western Indian state of Maharashtra, is home to Asia’s largest onion market and serves as a key centre for setting onion prices in India.
Millions of Hindus around the world will celebrate Deepavali, the annual festival of lights on Nov 8.
Demand is likely to soar for the reddish bulb, famous for its pungency, colour and long-shelf life. It is an important ingredient in every Indian cuisine.
India is one of the largest onion-growing countries in the world after China, with annual production of about 30 million tonnes. Last year, it exported about 1.5 million metric tonnes of fresh onions, according to India’s Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority.
Malaysia imports more than 50 per cent of its onion supply from India, with Maharashtra accounting for a large share of the shipments.
The state produces more than 50 per cent of India’s onion exports.
Indian consumers are currently paying about 60 Indian rupees (0.63 cents/RM2.56) per kg.
Export prices range from US$500 to US$700 per metric tonne (RM2,029 to RM2,841) for standard red onions, depending on the destination, say industry players.
“We are hoping to see crop growth post-Diwali (northern Indian pronunciation of Deepavali) as there has been some rainfall in recent days. We can only see better improvements in the next monsoon season, in July or August,” said Jagtap.
Production remains tight, and prices are volatile, while farmers are likely to face a financial crunch during the festival season.
“Around Diwali, the market is expected to remain sensitive to supply conditions. As fresh kharif arrivals increase, price pressures may ease. However, the extent of any price correction will depend on actual production, market arrivals and demand.
“Countries such as Malaysia that import Indian onions may face higher procurement costs if Indian wholesale and export prices remain elevated,” Sanjay Holkar, a leading exporter based in Nashik City in Maharashtra, told Bernama.
Indian Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution, in a statement dated Oct 9, said fresh kharif onions are beginning to arrive from major producing states — including Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Rajasthan, while availability from stored stocks continues to meet market demands.
“Arrivals from these producing regions are expected to increase further in the coming weeks, improving overall availability in the consuming markets during the upcoming festive season,” said the ministry.
In Kuala Lumpur, ahead of Deepavali, the Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry capped the prices of essential items including Australian dhal, grated coconut, large red onions and Indian shallots, from November 4 to 10.
Onion prices are currently costing about RM4 per kilogramme in local markets.
According to the Federal Agricultural Marketing Authority, Malaysians consume nearly 750,000 metric tonnes of onions annually. — Bernama

Title: Relief centre in Kerian closed as Perak recovers from floods
Article:
IPOH, Nov 1 — The only temporary relief centre (PPS) in the Kerian district, which was opened last Thursday to accommodate flood victims, was closed at noon today.
Kerian District Officer and Kerian District Disaster Management Committee chairman Saidi Shaari said monitoring found that conditions in the affected areas were now safe and all victims had been allowed to return to their respective homes.
“Our deepest appreciation and gratitude go to all government agencies and NGOs (non-governmental organisations) that assisted in and coordinated the smooth operation of the relief centre throughout its operation,” he said in a statement today.
Earlier this morning, 18 people from seven families were taking shelter at the Sekolah Kebangsaan Titi Serong relief centre. They were residents of Taman Aman Sejahtera and Taman Desa Aman 1. — Bernama

Title: Adly Zahari: Melaka election not a waste of time, public funds as ‘democratic power belongs to the people’
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 1 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) has dismissed claims that the 16th Melaka State Election is a waste of time and public funds, describing it instead as an important democratic process that allows the people to determine the mandate for the state government.
Melaka PH chairman Adly Zahari said the coalition was seeking the support of all Melakans, rather than relying solely on its own party members, to secure a mandate to govern the state.
Adly, who is also the PH candidate for the Bukit Katil state seat and an Amanah vice-president, said that while other political parties might be able to win by relying on their own supporters, PH believed its victory depended on the trust and support of the wider electorate.
“I do not deny that Barisan Nasional could win with the support of its own members. However, we in Pakatan Harapan are using this election to appeal to the people of Melaka for their support.
“We can only win with the support of the people of Melaka. Governing power is not a permanent right of any party, and voters do not owe their mandate to anyone. Ultimately, democratic power belongs to the people,” he said.
He was speaking at a daily press conference at the PH main operations room here today, which was also attended by Melaka DAP chairman Khoo Poay Tiong.
Meanwhile, Adly, who is also Deputy Defence Minister, said initial feedback gathered by PH’s 24 candidates during their campaign activities indicated that residents remained concerned about water bills, homeownership difficulties, access to welfare assistance and recurring floods.
He said small-scale traders were also facing challenges involving capital and rental costs.
Adly urged Barisan Nasional (BN), which won 21 of the 28 seats in the previous state election, to take responsibility for addressing these concerns and explain the measures taken, rather than behaving as though it had only recently assumed control of the state administration.
“...the people have every right to ask. If even basic matters remain unresolved and continue to be a source of public complaints, on what grounds should the current administration be praised? Signboards can be changed and slogans refreshed, but the quality of service must deliver the best possible outcomes for the people,” he said.
The Election Commission has set November 14 as polling day for the 16th Melaka State Election, while early voting is on November 10.
For the latest updates on the election, visit
https://election.bernama.com/prn/melaka/2026/
. — Bernama

Title: ‘Unfair and a bully’: Anthony Loke defends DAP rep and dares MCA chief to debate him instead
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 1 — DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke has challenged MCA president Wee Ka Siong to a public debate to compare their respective track records as the head of the Transport Ministry.
Loke, the current minister, simultaneously dismissed Wee's recent call for a debate between DAP’s Bandar Hilir incumbent, Leng Chau Yen, and her MCA challenger, Jasmine Lok.
The DAP leader accused the MCA chief of bullying, claiming Wee was attempting to exploit Leng’s speech impediment,
FMT
reported.
He stressed that her condition has never hindered her ability to serve the people of Bandar Hilir over the last five years.
“She has proven herself, she has been there for one term. So, why is Wee only singling her out? Why not other constituencies? He is being unfair and was trying to be a bully,” Loke told reporters at a press conference after officiating the Federal Territories DAP convention today.
Loke pivoted the confrontation toward his own performance, offering to face Wee directly.
“If he wishes for a debate, I can debate him anytime on transport issues,” he said.
Earlier, during his convention speech, Loke urged MCA to “take us on everywhere” if the party genuinely wanted to challenge DAP.
“I can also debate with (Wee). What did you do as transport minister compared with what I have done as transport minister? We are not afraid to be challenged,” he said.
Loke first held the transport portfolio from 2018 to 2020 before the Pakatan Harapan-led federal administration collapsed.
Wee took over the role until late 2022, and Loke was reappointed in December of that year following the formation of the unity government.

Title: Melaka polls: Run clean campaigns, steer clear of 3R issues, Teo Nie Ching tells candidates
Article:
KULAI, Nov 1 — Political parties and candidates contesting the upcoming Melaka State Election have been reminded not to issue or distribute materials touching on 3R (religion, race, and royalty) issues throughout the campaign period.
Deputy Communications Minister Teo Nie Ching said that while heated verbal exchanges may occur during campaigning, all quarters must run clean campaigns and steer clear of sensitive topics.
“I urge all political parties, candidates, and supporters involved not to put forward any materials touching on 3R issues. Let us run a clean campaign,” she said after attending the Bukit Permai state constituency Deepavali contribution presentation programme at the Arulmigu Mariamman Temple here today.
The Election Commission (EC) has set Nov 14 as polling day for the Melaka state election, with early voting on Nov 10.
Meanwhile, commenting on cybersecurity, Teo stressed that the recent system breach in Kluang should serve as a wake-up call to all government agencies and local authorities.
She said the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) had not received any formal request for assistance from the Kluang Municipal Council (MPK), but the commission stands ready to provide technical support, advice, and expertise if needed.
Teo also cautioned against taking cybersecurity lightly, given people’s high reliance on the internet and cloud computing.
“Do not assume hackers will not target our systems; the risk is real and very high,” she said, stressing the importance of allocating an adequate budget to strengthen cybersecurity and conduct regular security audits.
Earlier, video clips circulated on social media showing several public LED display screens in Kluang hacked by irresponsible individuals to display obscene content.
Following the incident, MPK said in a statement on Facebook that an investigation was underway with system vendors to identify the root cause, take corrective action, and enhance system security.
The municipal council apologised for the inconvenience and public concern, reiterating that it strongly condemned the act and would not hesitate to take legal action against anyone attempting to tarnish its reputation. — Bernama
